sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: When is the only situation you should move an injured crash victim?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Do not move an injured person unless another crash poses a danger.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: Why must you alert oncoming and approaching vehicles right after a collision?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Warn approaching traffic after a crash to prevent additional harm.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: Whose names and addresses should you gather at a crash scene?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Obtain names and addresses for the witnesses and the people involved in the crash.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: Which three personal and credential details must you record from the other driver?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Record the other driver's name, address and driver-license number.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: Which five details about the other vehicle should you write down after a crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Record the other vehicle's make, model, year, damage and license-plate number.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: What financial-responsibility detail must you record from the other driver at a crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: Record the other driver's insurance-company name.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Which three crash outcomes require you to contact law enforcement in Wyoming?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Contact police for a crash involving injury, death or at least one thousand dollars of property damage.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: When must you give your crash details to investigating police officers?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Provide police with crash information at the time of the crash.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: Who completes the official crash report and which WYDOT office receives it?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: Police complete and submit the crash report to WYDOT's Accident Records Section.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: What must you do first if you strike unattended property and cannot locate the owner?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: If unattended property is damaged and its owner cannot be found, leave a note where the owner can find it.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: Which five contact and credential items must appear on a note left on damaged unattended property?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: That unattended-property note must include your name, address, telephone, driver-license number and license-plate number.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: Besides your identity details, what three crash facts must an unattended-property note state?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: The unattended-property note must also state the crash date, time and vehicle damage.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: After leaving a complete note on damaged unattended property, whom else must you notify?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: After leaving the unattended-property information, also contact the nearest law-enforcement agency.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: What three actions may a police officer take if your vehicle appears to have unsafe equipment?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: A police officer may stop and inspect vehicle equipment, require immediate repair of defects and issue a fine if the vehicle is unsafe.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: Which five vehicle lighting systems must stay in proper working order?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: Required headlights, parking lights, brake lights, tail lights and turn signals must work properly.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: Which two braking systems on your vehicle must be kept in good operating condition?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: The vehicle's brakes and parking brake must be in good operating condition.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: Which three visibility, warning, and restraint items must function properly on your vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: Required mirrors, horn and safety belts must function properly.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: Which five glass, traction, and underbody components must remain in good condition?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: The required windshield, wipers, tires, muffler and exhaust system must be in good condition.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: Where do you look to find the correct inflation pressure recommended for your vehicle's tires?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: Use the recommended tire pressure from the vehicle owner's manual or driver-side door jamb.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: What tool should you use to check your tire inflation accurately?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: Measure tire pressure with a tire-pressure gauge.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: What should you do if your gauge reads higher than the door-jamb tire pressure recommendation?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: If measured pressure is above the door-jamb recommendation, release air until it matches.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: What should you do when measured tire pressure sits below your vehicle's recommended number?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: If pressure is below the vehicle recommendation, add air or seek tire-professional help to reach it.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: How often should you inspect your tires for tread wear and sidewall damage?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: Inspect tires for wear and damage monthly or before a long road trip.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: How do you hold and place a penny to check your tire tread depth?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: For the penny-test setup, hold the coin at Lincoln's body and insert his head into a groove where tread appears lowest.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: What visual result in the handbook's penny test means your tire tread passes?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: In the handbook's penny test, tread covering any part of Lincoln's head is the stated pass criterion.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.front: How does driving on tread shallower than the penny-test threshold affect your car?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.expected_back: Tread below the penny-test criterion reduces grip in adverse conditions.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: How do a motorcyclist's legal rights and duties compare with those of car and truck drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: Motorcyclists share the rights and responsibilities of other public-road users.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: What two visual challenges make motorcycles tricky for other drivers to read in traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: A motorcycle can be difficult to identify in traffic, and its distance or speed can be hard to judge.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: What must you do before turning left in front of an oncoming motorcycle?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: Before turning left ahead of an approaching motorcycle, look again and establish its speed.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.front: Why must you wait before pulling out ahead of a motorcycle displaying a turn signal?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.expected_back: Do not enter ahead of a signaling motorcycle until you know the rider is actually turning rather than continuing straight.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.front: Why might a motorcycle's turn signal keep flashing long after a lane change or turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.expected_back: Most motorcycle turn signals do not cancel automatically.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.front: May you drive alongside a motorcycle inside the same lane if the lane is wide or the rider hugs one edge?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.expected_back: A motorcycle is entitled to the full lane, so never move alongside it in the same lane even when the lane is wide or the rider is near one side.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.front: For what three reasons do motorcyclists intentionally shift left or right inside their lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.expected_back: Motorcyclists may change position within a lane to see, be seen or avoid objects near the road.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.front: Which six weather or roadway conditions can force a motorcyclist to adjust speed or direction suddenly?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.expected_back: Bad weather, slick pavement, crosswinds, rail crossings, metal bridges and grooves may cause a motorcycle to change speed or direction quickly.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.front: Must you yield to pedestrians in an intersection crosswalk area when no white lines are painted?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk area even when no pavement markings are present.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.front: What two adjustments should you make near schools when pedestrians are around?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.expected_back: Near schools, slow down and enlarge the space cushion when pedestrians are present.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.front: What unpredictable behavior must you anticipate from children near neighborhoods or schools?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.expected_back: Children near residential or school traffic may run into a vehicle's path unexpectedly.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.front: Which side of the road should you walk on if a breakdown forces you onto a road without sidewalks?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.expected_back: If a disabled vehicle forces you to walk where there is no sidewalk, walk on the road's left side facing traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F41.front: What clothing choice helps drivers spot you if you must walk along a road after dark?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.expected_back: Wear light-colored clothing when walking at night so drivers can see you more easily.

sec11-card-sec11-F42.front: What rights and duties apply to bicyclists, and where on the pavement must they normally ride?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.expected_back: Bicyclists share the public-road rights and duties of vehicle drivers and must ride as near the pavement's right side as practical and safe.

sec11-card-sec11-F43.front: Even though a car may legally fit beside a bicycle in one lane, what does the handbook advise?
sec11-card-sec11-F43.expected_back: Although a car may legally travel beside a bicycle in one lane, the handbook advises leaving more room instead.

sec11-card-sec11-F44.front: Which three roadside hazards might force a bicyclist to swerve suddenly into your path?
sec11-card-sec11-F44.expected_back: A cyclist may swerve to avoid a grate, road object or opening car door, so leave ample room while following or passing.

sec11-card-sec11-F45.front: What lighting equipment must a bicycle carry after dark, and what caution remains for drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-F45.memory_hook: Front light, rear reflectors, still dim
sec11-card-sec11-F45.expected_back: A bicycle used after dark must have a front light and rear reflectors, which can still be difficult for drivers to see.

sec11-card-sec11-F46.front: Where should you actively direct your eyes at night to avoid hitting poorly lit cyclists?
sec11-card-sec11-F46.expected_back: Watch the road edge for bicycles at night rather than relying only on their lights and reflectors.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: What maximum speed does a slow-moving-vehicle emblem tell you the vehicle ahead can travel?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: The slow-moving-vehicle symbol warns that the vehicle ahead cannot travel faster than twenty-five miles per hour

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: Do slow-moving farm or maintenance vehicles have a legal right to use public roadways?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: Slow-moving vehicles have a legal right to use the roadway, so respond patiently.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: In which five driving maneuvers do tractor-trailers handle very differently from passenger cars?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: Tractor-trailers behave differently from passenger cars when accelerating, braking, climbing, changing lanes or turning.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: Which active-light vehicles, speeds, and roadside positions trigger Wyoming's fuller Move Over rule?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: The fuller Move Over passage covers an emergency or authorized municipal, public-utility, construction or maintenance vehicle stopped or moving under twenty miles per hour on or within three feet of the roadway with warning lights or signals active.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: How soon must you carry out your Move Over lane change or slowdown once you spot a covered vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: The Move Over passage requires the applicable response as soon as it is safe.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: What happens if a police officer's hand or flare directions conflict with standard Move Over lane separation?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Police directions override the Move Over lane-separation instruction.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: On a highway with two or more same-direction lanes, where must you position your car under Move Over?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: For that provision on an interstate or other highway with at least two lanes in the warning vehicle's direction, merge to the farthest lane or leave at least one traffic lane of separation.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: On a two-lane road posted at 45 mph or higher, how much must you slow down for a Move Over vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: The later Move Over passage directs a driver on a two-lane road posted at forty-five miles per hour or above to travel twenty miles per hour below the posted limit unless police direct otherwise.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: Who can be injured or killed in a wildlife collision on rural Wyoming highways?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: Wildlife collisions on rural Wyoming roads can injure or kill vehicle occupants as well as animals.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: Although animal strikes occur all year, during which two seasons do they peak?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: Animal collisions can happen year-round but are most common during spring and fall migrations.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: How should you respond whenever you pass a yellow deer-crossing warning sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: Slow down and use extra caution where deer-crossing signs appear.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.front: Where should your eyes search when watching for wildlife along rural roads?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.expected_back: When watching for animals, scan the road ahead and both roadsides.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.front: How should you use your headlights at night to spot roadside animals earlier?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.expected_back: At night, use high beams when possible to illuminate the road and roadside while watching for animals.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.front: Which two natural landscape features call for extra wildlife alertness?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.expected_back: Be especially watchful for animals near forested areas and water.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.front: Which two times of day combine animal feeding movement with poor driver visibility?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.expected_back: Be particularly alert for animals at dawn and dusk, when feeding activity and reduced visibility coincide.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.front: What subtle visual glint ahead at night often reveals an animal before its body appears?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.expected_back: Watch for headlight reflections in animals' eyes ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.front: What three actions should you take when you spot an animal standing on or beside the road?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.expected_back: When an animal is on or near the road, slow down, tap the brakes to warn following drivers and sound the horn.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.front: When can you brake much harder for an animal in the road?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.expected_back: Harder braking for an animal is possible when no vehicle is following behind.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.front: Why shouldn't you flash your headlights at an animal standing in the roadway?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.expected_back: Flashing headlights at an animal can cause it to freeze in the roadway.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.front: What must you do, and avoid doing, if hitting an animal in your lane becomes unavoidable?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.expected_back: If an animal collision seems unavoidable, do not swerve suddenly; brake as quickly as safely possible while keeping control and staying on the road.

sec11-card-sec11-R21.front: Whom should you notify after hitting an animal, and when is reporting especially urgent?
sec11-card-sec11-R21.expected_back: Report an animal collision to local law enforcement, especially when the animal's body remains a hazard on the highway.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: How does defensive driving define a critical object?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: In defensive driving, a critical object is a person, vehicle, animal or other thing that may require a speed or direction change.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: How do you carry out the Identify step of defensive driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Identify critical objects by scanning for anything that may force a driving response.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: Once you identify a critical object, what mental forecast should you make?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: After identifying a critical object, predict what could happen and consider the worst plausible action described by the source.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: If you spot someone climbing into a parked car ten to fifteen seconds ahead, what should you prepare for?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: In the handbook's example, someone entering a parked car ten to fifteen seconds ahead prompts planning for a pullout without looking.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: What priority should guide every defensive-driving decision?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: Base a defensive-driving decision on preventing a crash rather than deciding who is right.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: What three qualities define a proper Execute maneuver in IPDE?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Execute the chosen response smoothly, predictably and early enough to avoid the crash.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: Where must you scan during IPDE driving, and what else must you do with surrounding motorists?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: IPDE driving requires scanning ahead and sideways and communicating with other drivers.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: Besides scanning and signaling, how does defensive driving manage space and competing hazards?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: Defensive driving also involves keeping space around the vehicle and separating or compromising risks when needed.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: How many seconds ahead of your vehicle does the handbook say you should scan?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: The handbook calls for scanning at least ten to fifteen seconds ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: How do you check in real time how many seconds ahead your eyes are scanning?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: To gauge forward scanning, choose a fixed roadside object and count seconds until reaching it.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: What count confirms you are looking far enough ahead during the forward-scan check?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: The source's forward-look check should allow counting beyond ten seconds before passing the chosen object.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: What environmental conditions, controls, and road users should your scan take in?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: Scan weather, traffic and road conditions as well as signs, signals, markings, vehicles and pedestrians.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: What bad habit usually explains why a driver keeps getting startled by sudden traffic events?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: Unexpected traffic surprises can indicate that a driver is not looking far enough ahead for critical objects.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: When should you classify people, vehicles, or animals off to the side of the road as critical objects?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: Treat roadside people, vehicles or animals as critical when they could enter your path or require a speed or lane-position change.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: What specific search should a school warning sign trigger immediately?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: A school sign should prompt a search for children who might run into the vehicle's path.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: Why is timing so critical when communicating your plans to other drivers?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: Communicate plans to other drivers early enough to help prevent a collision.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: How can making eye contact help when right-of-way feels unclear?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: Eye contact can help communicate with drivers or pedestrians where priority is uncertain.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: What message can clear hand motions send to another driver or pedestrian?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: Hand motions can communicate that you are yielding to another driver or pedestrian.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: What can your vehicle's placement inside a lane communicate to traffic around you?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Lane position can communicate an intended maneuver.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: How many seconds before a turn does the defensive-communication section say to signal?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: The communication guidance calls for hand or electrical signals at least four to five seconds before turning.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: What two things does touching the brake pedal lightly well ahead of a planned stop accomplish?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: A light brake touch activates brake lights and begins slowing well before a planned stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: How does getting into the proper turn lane well ahead of an intersection help other motorists?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Being in the correct lane well before a turn helps communicate the plan.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: How should you use the horn to let an unaware driver, cyclist, or walker know you are there?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: A brief horn tap can alert other road users to your presence.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: Where should you position your car relative to other vehicles so your presence is unmistakable?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Place the vehicle where other drivers can see it rather than in their blind spots.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: Why do defensive drivers keep a four-sided space cushion around the entire car?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: A space cushion ahead, behind and on both sides provides room to avoid others' mistakes.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: Why does the handbook measure following distance in seconds instead of car lengths?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: Measuring following space in seconds is easier and more accurate than estimating car lengths in the handbook's method.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: How do you start the fixed-point count to measure your following time behind a vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: For the following-time test, choose a fixed point and begin counting when the leading vehicle's rear bumper passes it.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: What does it mean if your front bumper reaches the reference mark before you finish counting two seconds?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: In the two-second following test, your front reaching the reference point before two seconds have elapsed means the gap is too short.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: How much following time does Wyoming's length formula require per twenty feet of vehicle length?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: The handbook requires at least two seconds of following interval for every twenty feet of vehicle length.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: What is the minimum baseline following interval for a standard passenger car in ideal conditions?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: For a passenger car, the stated baseline following interval is at least two seconds.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: Why must you add extra following time whenever towing a boat or utility trailer?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Towing a boat or trailer adds length and weight and therefore requires more following space.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: Which three driving conditions require doubling a car's following interval to four seconds?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: Double a car's following time to four seconds on wet roads, with a heavier-than-normal load or at night.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: How many seconds of following time should a passenger car keep on snow- and slush-covered roads?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: Triple car following time to six seconds on roads covered by snow and slush.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: How much following time should you maintain when ice covers the roadway?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: When ice covers the road, quadruple car following time to eight seconds.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: How does a tailgater behind your bumper limit your own emergency options ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: A tailgater reduces the leading driver's ability to slow rapidly for an emergency ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: Which three early cues should you use to warn a tailgater before slowing or turning?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: With a tailgater, communicate turns and slowing early through signals, brake lights and advance lane position.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: How should you adjust your front following distance when another driver is tailgating you?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: If followed too closely, increase the gap ahead to gain more response time and space.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: What simple lane move clears a tailgater off your bumper on a multilane highway?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: A driver being tailgated can move to the right lane on a multilane highway.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: How can easing your speed help deal with a tailgater?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: Reducing speed can encourage a tailgating driver to pass.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.front: How do vehicles or barriers on both sides limit your emergency choices?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.expected_back: Road users or objects on both sides can box a vehicle in, limiting responses ahead to speeding up or slowing down.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.front: What positioning mistake next to a bicyclist must you avoid?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.expected_back: Avoid staying alongside a bicyclist for a prolonged period.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.front: Why should you avoid cruising right next to cars in adjacent lanes on multilane streets?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.expected_back: Avoid traveling beside other vehicles on multilane streets to preserve side space.

sec12-card-sec12-R15.front: How much lateral separation should you maintain from oncoming vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.expected_back: Keep as much separation from oncoming traffic as possible.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.front: Which two blind-spot situations must you actively avoid in traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.expected_back: Avoid both occupying another driver's blind spot and leaving another vehicle in your own blind spot.

sec12-card-sec12-R17.front: How should you position your car when driving alongside a row of parked vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-R17.expected_back: Keep room between your vehicle and parked vehicles.

sec12-card-sec12-R18.front: How do defensive drivers handle two or more road hazards whenever possible?
sec12-card-sec12-R18.expected_back: When possible, separate risks by dealing with one at a time.

sec12-card-sec12-R19.front: In the handbook's oncoming-truck and roadside-jogger scenario, how do you avoid meeting both at once?
sec12-card-sec12-R19.expected_back: In the jogger-and-truck example, changing speed lets the driver pass the two hazards at different times.

sec12-card-sec12-R20.front: What kind of escape space does separating hazards open up for your vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-R20.expected_back: Separating risks creates side space for an emergency response.

sec12-card-sec12-R21.front: When two hazards cannot be separated in time, how do you allocate your space?
sec12-card-sec12-R21.expected_back: When risks cannot be separated, give the greatest danger the most space.

sec12-card-sec12-R22.front: Between oncoming cars on your left and a child bicyclist on your right, which is the greater danger and why?
sec12-card-sec12-R22.expected_back: In the two-lane example with oncoming cars left and a child bicyclist right, the child is the greater danger because of possible sudden movement.

sec12-card-sec12-R23.front: Where in your lane should you position your car when trapped between oncoming traffic and a child cyclist?
sec12-card-sec12-R23.expected_back: In that child-cyclist example, moving closer to the centerline creates a larger cushion on the right.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: Which four nighttime challenges combine after dark to demand sharper driver alertness?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Night driving combines reduced visibility, oncoming glare, crossing animals and eyestrain, requiring greater alertness.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: Between what exact evening and morning times does Wyoming law require headlights?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: Headlights are required from one-half hour after sunset through one-half hour before sunrise.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: At what forward sight distance do dim light or bad weather legally trigger headlight use?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: Headlights are also required when low light or adverse weather prevents clearly seeing people and vehicles one thousand feet ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: Why should you switch on low-beam headlights early as evening light begins to fade?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: Turn on low beams as daylight fades so other drivers can identify the vehicle and its actions.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: Can you legally drive with only your parking lights switched on when headlights are required?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Parking lights alone are not lawful when headlights are required.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: How should you adjust your following gap whenever darkness or weather cuts visibility?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: Increase following space when you cannot see clearly.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: Above what speed in the handbook's night illustration does stopping distance outrun headlight reach?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: In the handbook's night-driving illustration, traveling above fifty-five miles per hour exceeds the distance illuminated far enough ahead for a stop.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: Where do high beams belong at night, and which three situations call for low beams?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: Use high beams on rural highways and low beams when following, meeting oncoming traffic or driving in town.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: How many feet and roughly how many seconds before meeting an oncoming vehicle must you dim high beams?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: Dim headlights at least five hundred feet before meeting another vehicle; the handbook describes that as about four to five seconds.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: Within what distance behind a vehicle ahead must you switch headlights to their lowest beam?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: When approaching within three hundred feet behind another vehicle, dim headlights to the lowest beam.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: How must your low-beam headlights be aimed whenever you drive?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Low beams must be aimed to avoid glare at all times.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: How should you clean your windshield to cut nighttime glare from approaching headlights?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: Clean both sides of the windshield to reduce glare from oncoming vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: Why does wiping road grime off your headlight lenses matter before night travel?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: Clean headlights improve the light available for seeing ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: What happens if you lock your gaze onto your own bright headlight patch instead of moving your eyes?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: Keep the eyes moving rather than staring at the headlight spot, which can contribute to eyestrain, fatigue and poor concentration.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: What roadside hazards and cross-street clues should you actively scan for after dark?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: At night, scan for animals, pedestrians and bicycles and look sideways for lights from vehicles entering or crossing ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: What two clues can you read by watching the lights of vehicles traveling ahead of you at night?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: Check the lights of vehicles ahead for signs of speed or lane-position changes.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: Which headlight setting belongs in fog, and what auxiliary front lamps can help?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: Use low-beam headlights in fog; front fog lights may sometimes help.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: When is it appropriate to switch on bright red rear fog lights?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: Use red rear fog lights only in heavy fog or similar hazardous weather that seriously reduces visibility.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: What must you do with rear fog lights as soon as visibility clears up?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: Switch rear fog lights off once visibility improves.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: What must you monitor around you while trimming your normal speed in fog?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: Reduce normal speed in fog while watching the difference from surrounding traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: A speed gap above how many miles per hour from surrounding traffic creates high crash danger in fog?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: The fog discussion warns of high crash risk when speed differs from other traffic by more than fifteen miles per hour

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: What should you do if dense fog threatens to create a wide speed mismatch with surrounding traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: Stop at the nearest safe location if fog could create a large speed difference from other traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: When fog cuts forward sight below how many seconds ahead should you consider pulling off to stop?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: If fog prevents seeing at least ten seconds ahead, consider pulling off at the nearest safe place and stopping.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: What targets should you scan for in poor visibility while maximizing your space cushion?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: In poor visibility, scan for vehicle lights, pedestrians and stopped or slow vehicles while enlarging the space cushion as much as possible.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: Why must you lower your speed as soon as pavement turns slick?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: Slow down on slippery pavement because stopping distance increases.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.front: How many seconds of following distance should a passenger car keep in rain?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.expected_back: In rain, double a car's following interval to four seconds.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.front: Which headlight beam should you run whenever driving through rain?

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: What visual sign on your glass tells you it is time for new wiper blades?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: Replace wiper blades if they smear or streak the windshield.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.front: Why is the first thirty minutes of a rainstorm especially slick on paved roads?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.expected_back: Use extra care during the first half hour of rain, when dust and oil mix with water and make the road slippery.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.front: What physically happens beneath your tires when a car begins hydroplaning?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.expected_back: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a thin water film rather than the pavement.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.front: What straightforward driver adjustment helps keep tires from hydroplaning in rain?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.expected_back: Slowing down helps prevent hydroplaning during rain.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.front: What traction equipment does the handbook recommend for snow and ice to cut skids and braking distance?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.expected_back: The snow-and-ice guidance recommends snow tires or chains to resist skidding and reduce stopping distance.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.front: What kinds of throttle, brake, or wheel inputs must you avoid on snow or ice?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.expected_back: On snow or ice, avoid sudden speed or direction changes.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.front: Which two roadway spots freeze earliest and hold black ice longest?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.expected_back: Watch for ice on bridges and shaded road areas.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.front: To how many seconds does the handbook triple a passenger car's forward cushion on snow?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.expected_back: For snow, the source triples a car's forward cushion to six seconds.

sec13-card-sec13-F36.front: To how many seconds does the handbook quadruple a passenger car's forward cushion on ice?
sec13-card-sec13-F36.expected_back: For ice, the source quadruples a car's forward cushion to eight seconds.

sec13-card-sec13-F37.front: Why must you scrape and defog all vehicle windows rather than peeking through a tiny porthole?
sec13-card-sec13-F37.expected_back: Keep vehicle windows clear to see and communicate with other road users.

sec13-card-sec13-F38.front: How should you shed speed before reaching a stop or turn on snow or ice?
sec13-card-sec13-F38.expected_back: On snow or ice, slow gradually and smoothly before stopping or turning.

sec13-card-sec13-F39.front: Why must you keep your wheels from locking up during winter braking?
sec13-card-sec13-F39.expected_back: Avoid locking the wheels because steering control depends on their rotation.

sec13-card-sec13-F40.front: What rule applies to using cruise control on snow-packed or icy roads?
sec13-card-sec13-F40.expected_back: Do not use cruise control on snow or ice.

sec13-card-sec13-F41.front: Which vehicles face the greatest danger in strong Wyoming winds, and what is the primary defense?
sec13-card-sec13-F41.expected_back: Wind is particularly hazardous for trucks, recreational vehicles, campers and trailer-towing drivers, and lower speed is the source's recommended defense.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: What steering surprise should you brace for when emerging from a canyon, cut, or overpass into open plain?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: After leaving a wind-protected area for open space, be ready to correct steering as wind changes.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: How can passing or meeting a large semi-truck or bus affect your steering in windy conditions?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: Meeting a large truck or bus can bring sudden wind changes requiring steering corrections.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: When do crosswind gusts pose an extra-high threat to lane control?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: Be especially alert to wind effects on wet or slippery surfaces.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: What two steps does the handbook advise whenever a Wyoming blizzard threatens?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: Avoid driving in a blizzard whenever possible and obtain local severe-weather information.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: Why must you stay with your car rather than walking away if stranded or ditched in a blizzard?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: If stranded or ditched during a blizzard, stay with the vehicle so rescuers can locate you more easily.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: How should you set a window if trapped inside a vehicle during a blizzard?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: While stranded in a blizzard, leave a window open slightly for fresh air.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: How should you run the engine for warmth while stranded in snow, and what outside check is critical?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: Run the engine and heater sparingly with an open window, and ensure snow is not blocking the exhaust pipe.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: What physical habit inside a stranded winter vehicle helps keep your body warm?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: While stranded, move the arms and legs periodically rather than remaining in one position.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: Which two vehicle lights help plows and rescuers spot a stranded car, including after dark?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: Use emergency flashers to make a stranded vehicle visible and switch on the dome light at night.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.front: If multiple occupants are stranded together in a blizzard, how should they handle sleep?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.expected_back: When several people are stranded together, take turns watching rather than all sleeping at once.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.front: What two physical dangers must stranded drivers avoid during a winter storm?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.expected_back: Avoid overexertion and overexposure while stranded in a blizzard.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.front: With conventional non-anti-lock brakes, how should you work the pedal when an emergency crash looms?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.expected_back: For conventional braking in an imminent-crash response, pump the brakes to preserve control and steering.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.front: What happens if you stomp and hold unchanging hard pressure on conventional non-anti-lock brakes?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.expected_back: Hard, unchanging pressure on conventional brakes can cause a skid.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.front: How should you press an anti-lock brake pedal during an emergency stop, and why?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.expected_back: With anti-lock brakes, use hard, steady pedal pressure because the system adjusts automatically.

sec13-card-sec13-R15.front: Toward which side should you generally steer if an unavoidable head-on crash threatens?
sec13-card-sec13-R15.expected_back: If collision cannot otherwise be avoided, turn away from a head-on impact, generally to the right and off the roadway if necessary.

sec13-card-sec13-R16.front: Why does the evasive turn-away guidance warn against braking while steering hard away?
sec13-card-sec13-R16.expected_back: The turn-away guidance advises avoiding braking during the evasive turn to reduce skid risk.

sec13-card-sec13-R17.front: When can accelerating help avoid a side or rear collision, and what comes right after?
sec13-card-sec13-R17.expected_back: For a collision threat from the side or rear, accelerate only if room exists, then slow again after the danger passes.

sec13-card-sec13-R18.front: If a collision cannot be prevented at all, what impact angle is safer than hitting head-on?
sec13-card-sec13-R18.expected_back: When an impact is unavoidable, favor a glancing collision over a head-on impact.

sec13-card-sec13-R19.front: If you are forced to hit a roadside object to escape a worse crash, what kind should you aim for?
sec13-card-sec13-R19.expected_back: If an object must be struck, the handbook favors something more likely to give way.

sec13-card-sec13-R20.front: Where must your eyes and primary focus stay if your accelerator pedal sticks down?
sec13-card-sec13-R20.expected_back: If the accelerator sticks, concentrate on steering and keep looking at the road.

sec13-card-sec13-R21.front: If lifting a stuck gas pedal with your toe fails, how do you cut engine power from the wheels?
sec13-card-sec13-R21.expected_back: Try freeing a stuck accelerator with the foot; if unsuccessful, use the clutch or shift to neutral.

sec13-card-sec13-R22.front: Once neutral frees you from a stuck throttle, when do you switch off the ignition?
sec13-card-sec13-R22.expected_back: For a stuck accelerator, brake to a stop at the nearest safe location and switch off the ignition.

sec13-card-sec13-R23.front: What follow-up step is essential before driving normally again after a throttle sticks?
sec13-card-sec13-R23.expected_back: Have the sticking-accelerator cause identified and repaired.

sec13-card-sec13-R24.front: What immediate mental response is essential the moment your tires start skidding?
sec13-card-sec13-R24.expected_back: In a skid, stay calm and avoid overreacting.

sec13-card-sec13-R26.front: Why does the handbook split skid instructions into two separate sections?
sec13-card-sec13-R26.expected_back: The source explicitly distinguishes its conventional-brake skid procedure from ABS procedures.

sec13-card-sec13-R25.front: In a conventional-brake skid caused by hard braking or heavy gas, what pedal move comes first?
sec13-card-sec13-R25.expected_back: In the conventional-brake skid procedure, ease off hard braking or excessive acceleration if that action started the skid.

sec13-card-sec13-R27.front: How should you steer while recovering from a skid?
sec13-card-sec13-R27.expected_back: During skid recovery, steer to keep the vehicle aligned with the road and avoid oversteering.

sec13-card-sec13-R28.front: What steering adjustment must you prepare for right as a skid straightens out?
sec13-card-sec13-R28.expected_back: As the skid ends, be ready to steer in the opposite direction.

sec13-card-sec13-R29.front: Where should you look for specific skid-handling nuances on a front-wheel-drive vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-R29.expected_back: Consult the owner's manual for special front-wheel-drive skid instructions.

sec13-card-sec13-R30.front: What three-part move sums up handling an anti-lock brake emergency?
sec13-card-sec13-R30.expected_back: In an ABS emergency, press firmly, keep pressure on the pedal and steer out of danger.

sec13-card-sec13-R31.front: When should you figure out whether the car you are driving has anti-lock or conventional brakes?
sec13-card-sec13-R31.expected_back: Know which braking system the vehicle has before applying its emergency procedure.

sec13-card-sec13-R32.front: What gearshift and path choices help slow a vehicle if normal foot brakes fail?
sec13-card-sec13-R32.expected_back: The brake-failure procedure calls for a lower gear and finding an off-roadway place to slow and stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R33.front: Why must you keep holding the release lever or button when applying a manual parking brake during brake failure?
sec13-card-sec13-R33.expected_back: When using a release-equipped parking brake during brake failure, hold the release so braking can be eased if the rear wheels lock and a skid begins.

sec13-card-sec13-R34.front: Once you bring a car with failed brakes to a stop, may you limp it carefully to a repair shop?
sec13-card-sec13-R34.expected_back: Do not continue driving to a garage after brake failure.

sec13-card-sec13-R35.front: What is your immediate steering priority the instant a tire blows out?
sec13-card-sec13-R35.expected_back: After a tire blowout, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle traveling straight.

sec13-card-sec13-R36.front: How should you handle the gas and brake pedals right after a tire blows out?
sec13-card-sec13-R36.expected_back: For a blowout, ease off the accelerator without immediately applying the brakes.

sec13-card-sec13-R37.front: When is it safe to apply gentle braking and leave the lane after a blowout?
sec13-card-sec13-R37.expected_back: Once control returns after a blowout, brake gently and pull off at the nearest safe location.

sec13-card-sec13-R38.front: What reminder applies when jacking up and changing a blown tire beside a road?
sec13-card-sec13-R38.expected_back: Use caution when changing a tire after a blowout.

sec13-card-sec13-R39.front: What first warning and speed steps should you take if an oncoming vehicle drifts into your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R39.expected_back: If an oncoming vehicle enters your lane, slow and try to warn its driver with headlight flashes.

sec13-card-sec13-R40.front: Where should you position your car if a wrong-way driver keeps closing in your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R40.expected_back: If the oncoming vehicle continues toward you, move as far right as possible.

sec13-card-sec13-R41.front: If an oncoming vehicle still stays in your path and impact threatens, where do you steer?
sec13-card-sec13-R41.expected_back: If that vehicle still approaches and collision threatens, steer off the roadway to the right.

sec13-card-sec13-R42.front: Why must you never twist the ignition key to the lock position while your vehicle is rolling?
sec13-card-sec13-R42.expected_back: With a steering-lock device, never turn the ignition key to LOCK while moving because steering can lock and control can be lost.

sec13-card-sec13-R43.front: If your right wheels drop off the paved edge onto a rough shoulder, what immediate posture keeps control?
sec13-card-sec13-R43.expected_back: After running off the pavement, keep calm, hold the wheel firmly and prepare for sudden shocks.

sec13-card-sec13-R44.front: While stabilizing after your wheels leave the pavement, where should you steer and what do you do with the gas?
sec13-card-sec13-R44.expected_back: While recovering from leaving the pavement, remain on the shoulder and ease off the accelerator.

sec13-card-sec13-R45.front: How should you use the brakes while rolling straight along an unpaved shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-R45.expected_back: Brake gently and reduce speed gradually while on the shoulder.

sec13-card-sec13-R46.front: Once you have slowed down on the shoulder, what must you check before steering back onto the highway?
sec13-card-sec13-R46.expected_back: After slowing on the shoulder, check traffic behind and ahead before returning toward the roadway.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: Which fleet types count as authorized emergency vehicles under the Wyoming glossary?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: Authorized emergency vehicles include fire, police and ambulance vehicles and others authorized by statute.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: How does the glossary define a bicycle, and what wheeled devices does it leave out?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: The glossary defines a bicycle as a human-powered vehicle with two tandem wheels, excluding scooters and similar devices.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: How does the Wyoming handbook classify bicycles when operating on public roads?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: The handbook classifies bicycles as vehicles that may use Wyoming public roads.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: Are bicycle helmets legally mandatory in Wyoming, and what headgear standard does the handbook recommend?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: The handbook recommends a correctly fitted, Consumer Product Safety Certified bicycle helmet even though it says a helmet is not legally required.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: Where around your vehicle do glossary blind spots hide from your rearview mirrors?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: The glossary's blind spots lie near the rear corners on both sides and are not visible in rearview mirrors.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.front: What physical move must you make to check the blind-spot areas beside your vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.expected_back: Turn the head to view the glossary's blind-spot areas.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: How does the glossary define a crosswalk?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: A crosswalk is a place where people may legally cross a street or highway.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: Does a legal crosswalk always require painted white stripes on the pavement?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: A crosswalk may be marked or unmarked.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.front: How do you picture the boundaries of an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.expected_back: For an unmarked crosswalk, the glossary uses imaginary lines connecting sidewalks across the roadway.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.front: What does the glossary mean by a traffic gap?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.expected_back: A traffic gap is enough open space between vehicles for another vehicle to enter safely.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.front: In straightforward glossary terms, what is a helmet?

sec15-card-sec15-R05.front: What is a No-Zone around a large truck or heavy vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.expected_back: A No-Zone is a heavy vehicle's side or directly rearward area where another vehicle is invisible to its driver.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: Who is a self-propelled pedestrian vehicle exclusively built to serve?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: A pedestrian vehicle is self-propelled equipment designed exclusively for people with a physical disability.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.front: What maximum width in inches does the glossary set for a pedestrian vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.expected_back: The glossary limits pedestrian-vehicle width to forty-eight inches.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: What do the letters B A C stand for, and what does the term measure?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: BAC stands for Blood Alcohol Concentration and refers to alcohol in the bloodstream.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: How does the glossary define vehicle brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: Brakes are the devices used to stop a vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: What makes a person, animal, or vehicle ahead count as a critical object?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: A critical object is anything that could require slowing, accelerating or turning, including a person, vehicle or animal.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.front: What offense does Wyoming's D W U I abbreviation describe?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.expected_back: DWUI means operating a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.front: According to the glossary, what are your tires riding on during hydroplaning?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.expected_back: Hydroplaning means the tires ride on a thin water layer instead of the road.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.front: How does the glossary define an intersection?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.expected_back: An intersection is the area where streets or highways meet or cross.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.front: How many lines of vehicles is a single roadway lane built to carry?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.expected_back: A lane is a roadway section for one line of vehicles.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.front: What does a highway median separate, and what materials can form it?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.expected_back: A median separates roadways and may consist of grass, concrete or other material.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.front: May a driver cut across, ride on, or drive over a highway median?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.expected_back: Riding on, over or across a median is unlawful under the glossary's rule.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.front: When does merging traffic happen, and what classic highway spot illustrates it?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.expected_back: Merging traffic occurs when two moving traffic lanes come together, such as at an interstate entrance.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.front: What power source and transport role define a motor vehicle on public highways?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.expected_back: A motor vehicle is self-propelled by power other than human muscle and transports people or property on public highways.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.front: Does the glossary count motorcycles and mopeds as motor vehicles?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.expected_back: The glossary includes motorcycles and mopeds as motor vehicles.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.front: What makes an offense count as a moving violation on your driving record?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.expected_back: A moving violation involves control or lack of control while a motor vehicle is moving and results in a conviction.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.front: Which two license-restriction breaches can trigger a moving-violation conviction?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.expected_back: A moving-violation conviction can include driving contrary to a corrective-lens or outside-mirror restriction.

sec15-card-sec15-R19.front: Which three sequential stages combine to make up total stopping distance?
sec15-card-sec15-R19.expected_back: Total stopping distance includes travel while deciding to stop, reacting and braking until the vehicle fully stops.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: What wheel count, weight range, ID mark, and seat height define a Wyoming multipurpose vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: The multipurpose-vehicle definition requires an identifying number, at least four wheels, weight from three hundred to three thousand pounds and a permanent upright seat at least twenty-four inches above ground.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: What registration and tag rule applies before operating a multipurpose vehicle on streets or highways?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: A multipurpose vehicle must be registered and plated for street or highway operation.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: Which highways ban multipurpose vehicles, and what special rules govern them?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: A multipurpose vehicle may not operate on interstate highways and is subject to slow-moving-vehicle requirements.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: Which Wyoming driver-license classes authorize operating a multipurpose vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: The handbook permits a multipurpose vehicle to be driven under any driver-license class.

sec15-card-sec15-R14.front: Which specific part of a street or highway corridor counts as the roadway?
sec15-card-sec15-R14.expected_back: A roadway is the street or highway portion ordinarily used for driving.

sec15-card-sec15-R15.front: Where does a highway shoulder sit, and what two surfaces might it have?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.expected_back: The shoulder lies beside the traveled highway and can be paved or gravel.

sec15-card-sec15-R16.front: Which two practical functions does a highway shoulder serve?
sec15-card-sec15-R16.expected_back: A shoulder accommodates stopped vehicles and helps highway drainage.

sec15-card-sec15-R17.front: In which directions around your car does a proper space cushion protect you?
sec15-card-sec15-R17.expected_back: A space cushion separates the vehicle from others ahead, behind and beside it.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.front: At what minimum age and under which three life statuses does a teen qualify as an emancipated minor?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.expected_back: The glossary's emancipated minor is at least seventeen and is or was married, serves in the United States military, or has district-court emancipation.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.front: How does a qualifying teen have emancipated status placed onto a Wyoming license?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.expected_back: An emancipated minor may request that status on a Wyoming license by applying to the department and paying the required fee.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.front: What payment is mandatory before a suspended or revoked license privilege can be restored?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.expected_back: A reinstatement fee is required before a suspension or revocation can be lifted and the driving privilege restored.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.front: Staying in Wyoming for at least how many days triggers the presence clause of residency?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.expected_back: The residency definition's presence clause specifies one hundred twenty days or more in the jurisdiction.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.front: How does registering to vote in Wyoming affect your driver-licensing resident status?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.expected_back: Being registered to vote in Wyoming is an alternative included in the handbook's resident definition.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.front: How does applying for state public assistance affect whether Wyoming counts you as a resident?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.expected_back: Applying for public assistance from Wyoming is an alternative included in the resident definition.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.front: Which outdoor recreation credentials also classify the holder as a Wyoming resident in the handbook?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.expected_back: Holding a valid Wyoming resident hunting or fishing license is another stated resident-definition alternative.

sec15-card-sec15-R13.front: What does revocation do to your privilege to drive?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.expected_back: Revocation terminates the privilege to drive.

sec15-card-sec15-R18.front: How does suspension differ from revocation, and how do privileges come back?
sec15-card-sec15-R18.expected_back: Suspension temporarily removes driving privileges, with return possible after time, specified requirements or both.

sec15-card-sec15-R20.front: Which Wyoming state agency oversees driver licensing?
sec15-card-sec15-R20.expected_back: WYDOT is the state agency responsible for Wyoming driver licensing.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.front: Why do standardized sign shapes and background colors matter when snow, glare, or distance blurs text?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.expected_back: Sign shapes and colors communicate meaning even when the lettering is difficult to read.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.front: What core guidance do painted pavement markings give a driver?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.expected_back: Pavement markings provide information about a vehicle's proper road position.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.front: What is the legal force of regulatory traffic signs?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.expected_back: Regulatory signs instruct drivers what to do and must be obeyed.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.front: How many sides form an octagon, and which single traffic sign owns it?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.expected_back: An octagon has eight sides and is reserved for stop signs.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.front: What kind of stop does a red stop sign legally demand?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.expected_back: A stop sign requires a complete stop.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.front: What action does a downward-pointing triangular sign require toward intersecting or merging vehicles?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.expected_back: A downward-pointing triangle requires yielding to cross traffic or merging traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.front: What is the main job of roadway warning signs?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.expected_back: Warning signs alert drivers to conditions ahead.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.front: What geometric outline do most roadway warning signs use?

sec16-card-sec16-F09.front: Which kinds of roadway situations can warning signs highlight for extra driver attention?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.expected_back: Warning signs may identify road hazards, construction, schools or other conditions needing special attention.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.front: How do ordinary warning-sign colors differ from construction and maintenance warnings?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.expected_back: Most warning signs are yellow, while construction and maintenance warnings are orange.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.front: Which two core traffic behaviors do rectangular regulatory signs govern?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.expected_back: Rectangular regulatory signs direct traffic speed or direction.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.front: What does a yellow diamond with black symbols or lettering announce?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.expected_back: Yellow diamonds with black lettering warn of possible danger ahead.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.front: Which two school-related areas are marked by a five-sided pentagon sign?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.expected_back: A pentagon warns of a school zone or marks a school crossing.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.front: What roadway restriction begins right where a pennant-shaped sign stands?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.expected_back: A pennant-shaped sign marks the beginning of a no-passing zone.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.front: Which specific crossing ahead is announced by a round warning sign?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.expected_back: A round warning sign indicates a railroad crossing ahead.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.front: Which painted pavement markings can appear on the lane approaching railroad tracks?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.expected_back: A railroad approach may have a painted stop line or an X with the letters RR.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.front: How can highway engineers combine warnings on the approach to a railroad crossing?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.expected_back: Railroad approach warnings can use a combination of the listed signs and pavement markings.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.front: What text and background colors appear on construction signs?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.expected_back: Construction signs use black lettering on an orange background.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.front: What kind of conditions do construction and maintenance signs warn drivers to expect?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.expected_back: Construction and maintenance signs warn of temporary danger or unusual conditions.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.front: What is the purpose of the Emergency Notification Sign posted at a railroad crossing?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.expected_back: An Emergency Notification Sign, or ENS, is for crossing emergencies that may require train traffic to stop.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.front: Which two crossing problems does the handbook give as examples for using the Emergency Notification Sign?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.expected_back: Track obstructions and malfunctioning crossing lights or gates are examples of emergencies addressed by an ENS.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.front: What three pieces of navigation help do highway guide signs give motorists?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.expected_back: Guide signs tell drivers their location, road and route toward a destination.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.front: While most guide signs use rectangles, which two marker types can wear distinct shapes?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.expected_back: Most guide signs are rectangular, but county-road signs and freeway route markers may have different shapes.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.front: What determines whether a guide sign uses green, blue, or brown?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.expected_back: A guide sign's information type determines its color in the source description.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.front: Where must you bring your vehicle to a halt at a steady red traffic light?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.expected_back: At a red light, stop behind the crosswalk or stop line.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.front: When is turning right on a steady red light lawful in Wyoming?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.expected_back: A right turn on red is allowed only after stopping and yielding to people and other vehicles, unless a sign prohibits it.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.front: Under what exact street pairing does Wyoming permit a left turn on a red light?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.expected_back: A left turn on red from a one-way street to another one-way street is permitted after stopping and yielding.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.front: How should you respond when a traffic signal turns steady amber?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.expected_back: At an amber light, stop before entering the intersection if that can be done safely; otherwise proceed carefully.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.front: What clearance and yielding rules apply before driving into an intersection on a green light?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.expected_back: A green light permits entering only when the way is clear, while yielding to people and vehicles already in the intersection.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.front: Which roadside sign shares the exact same legal requirement as a flashing red signal?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.expected_back: A flashing red signal requires a complete stop before the intersection and has the same meaning as a stop sign.

sec16-card-sec16-R12.front: What does a flashing amber traffic signal require at an intersection or hazard spot?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.expected_back: A flashing amber signal requires caution at the warned hazardous intersection or location.

sec16-card-sec16-R13.front: What movement is barred when a traffic signal displays a lighted red arrow?
sec16-card-sec16-R13.expected_back: A red arrow prohibits turning in the direction it points.

sec16-card-sec16-R14.front: Which signal often precedes an amber arrow, and what does the amber arrow warn drivers to do?
sec16-card-sec16-R14.expected_back: An amber arrow may follow a green arrow and warns drivers to clear the intersection.

sec16-card-sec16-R15.front: How may you turn on a green arrow, and who still holds right-of-way inside the intersection?
sec16-card-sec16-R15.expected_back: A green arrow permits turning in its direction without stopping when the path is clear, but drivers must yield to people and other traffic already inside the intersection.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: What two dangerous braking behaviors can happen right after your brakes get soaked?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: Wet brakes may pull the vehicle sideways or provide less holding force than normal.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: What quick system check should you run right after driving through deep standing water?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: Test the brakes after driving through deep water.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: How do you dry wet brakes safely so normal stopping power returns?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: Use several gentle brake applications until wet brakes dry and work properly.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: If mechanical trouble forces you to stop along a road, where must your tires sit?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: If a malfunction requires stopping, put all four wheels on the shoulder.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: Which lights should you switch on immediately after pulling onto the shoulder with a breakdown?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: After a breakdown stop, turn on the four-way emergency flashers.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: Through which side should occupants step out of a disabled car parked on a shoulder?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: Leave a disabled vehicle from the side away from traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: Which visual signals on a disabled car tell passing patrols or motorists that you need assistance?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: For a vehicle problem, a white cloth on an antenna or door handle and a raised hood or trunk can signal the need for help.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: What does the handbook say about walking down an interstate highway to find help after breaking down?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: Do not walk for help after an interstate breakdown.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: Why should you move into a left lane whenever possible while passing a disabled vehicle on the shoulder?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: When passing a disabled vehicle on the shoulder, move left if possible because its driver may open a door or enter traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: Why is carbon monoxide gas impossible to detect by sight or smell?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: Carbon monoxide is poisonous and has neither color nor odor.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: Which physical warning signs does the handbook link to possible carbon-monoxide poisoning?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: The handbook lists yawning, fatigue, headache, dizziness, nausea and ringing ears as possible carbon-monoxide warning signs.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: What two immediate steps must you take if cabin symptoms point to carbon-monoxide exposure?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: If those symptoms suggest carbon-monoxide exposure, stop the engine and open windows for fresh air.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: What routine maintenance check guards against carbon monoxide entering your car?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: Have the exhaust system checked regularly for leaks.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: Why should you avoid sitting parked for long stretches with the motor idling?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: Avoid remaining parked for long periods with the engine running.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: What strict rule applies to starting or warming up a vehicle inside a shut garage?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: Never start or warm an engine in a closed garage.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: What assumption should you make every single time you approach railroad tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: Expect a train at every highway-rail crossing.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: Before rolling onto railroad tracks, what space check on the other side is mandatory?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Do not enter railroad tracks until sure the vehicle can clear the far side without stopping.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: When lowered crossing arms close the road, what two things must happen before you drive forward?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: Closed railroad gates mean the road is closed; wait until gates rise and red lights stop flashing before proceeding.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: Is driving around a lowered railroad crossing gate ever permitted?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: Never drive around a lowered railroad gate.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: At a crossing with more than one set of rails, what check comes before pulling out?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: At a multiple-track crossing, look and listen for another train from either direction before crossing.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: What is your very first priority if your vehicle stalls right on railroad tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: If a vehicle stalls on the tracks, immediately move everyone out and far from the tracks.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: Why must you never try restarting or pushing a stalled car off tracks with passengers still seated inside?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: Do not attempt to restart or push a vehicle off railroad tracks while passengers remain inside.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: Which emergency number should you dial immediately once everyone is clear of a car stalled on tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: Call nine one one to report a stalled-vehicle emergency at a railroad crossing.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: Which two risky maneuvers are strictly off-limits at a railroad crossing?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: Never race a train to a crossing or pass another vehicle at the crossing.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: Once a construction flag person halts your lane, when may you start rolling again?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: When a construction flag person orders a stop, wait until that person directs you to proceed.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: How should you adjust speed and visual scanning inside an active construction zone?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: Travel slowly through construction areas and watch for workers or equipment entering traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: Should you relax your caution in a signed work zone when no crews seem to be working?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: Maintain extra caution in a work zone even when no work appears active nearby.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: Why is sprinting past a semi-truck and darting in ahead of it before a work-zone taper so dangerous?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: Passing a truck fast before a work zone and cutting back in can force emergency braking and cause a rear-end crash if space is inadequate.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: Which non-motorized road users count as pedestrians under the handbook definition?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: Pedestrians include walkers, joggers, skaters and wheelchair users traveling without a motor vehicle or bicycle.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: In which five neighborhood or town settings should you expect frequent pedestrian activity?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: Expect frequent pedestrian encounters in business, residential, school, park and shopping areas.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: How much should you lower speed in areas where pedestrians are likely to appear?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: Where pedestrian encounters are likely, reduce speed enough to preserve sight distance for a response.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: During which maneuvers and street transitions must you yield right-of-way to pedestrians?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians at intersections, while turning, changing lanes or passing, and when entering or leaving a public roadway.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: Why can swerving violently to miss an animal on the highway be worse than hitting it?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: An animal-avoidance action that loses vehicle control may endanger occupants and nearby road users more than striking the animal.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.front: If striking a deer or other animal becomes unavoidable, what must stay your top priority throughout?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.expected_back: If an animal collision occurs, concentrate on control before, during and after impact.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: How must a responsible driver handle personal physical or mental limitations?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: Recognize personal driving limitations and compensate for them or avoid driving while impaired.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: How does losing emotional self-control behind the wheel affect your driving safety?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: Losing emotional self-control while driving increases errors and crash risk.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: What should you do when intense feelings overwhelm your ability to stay composed?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: Do not drive when overwhelming emotion prevents self-control.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: Which two core driving skills suffer when strong grief, rage, or terror takes over?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: Strong grief, rage or terror can interfere with identifying hazards and making sound decisions.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: Can even everyday mild emotions affect safe driving?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: Even mild emotion can distract from driving, which requires full attention.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: How does clear central vision support the safe-driving decision chain?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: Clear vision helps identify critical objects early enough to predict, decide and respond.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: What specific danger does healthy side vision help a driver catch?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: Side vision helps detect objects entering from the sides.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: Why does accurate distance judgment matter behind the wheel?

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: Which two separate nighttime visual abilities does the handbook highlight as part of good vision?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: Night vision and recovery after headlight glare are distinct parts of the source's good-vision description.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: How can drivers compensate when their eyes struggle to focus clearly at distance?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: Glasses or contact lenses can compensate for difficulty seeing clearly.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: How must a driver with reduced side vision compensate, especially before changing lanes?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: A driver with poor side vision must move the head as well as the eyes and be especially careful with shoulder checks before lane changes.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.front: What does the handbook instruct if a vision limitation cannot be safely overcome?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.expected_back: If a vision limitation cannot be adequately compensated, the source directs the person to stop driving.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.front: What two spacing adjustments help a driver who struggles with distance judgment?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.expected_back: Poor distance judgment calls for more following room and extra passing clearance.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.front: Poor distance judgment makes it harder to predict traffic events how many seconds ahead?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.expected_back: The source connects poor distance judgment with difficulty predicting events ten to fifteen seconds ahead.

sec14-card-sec14-R15.front: While slowing down at night helps weak night vision, driving how much slower than traffic creates its own hazard?
sec14-card-sec14-R15.expected_back: Slower night driving can compensate for poor night vision, but being ten to fifteen miles per hour below other traffic may itself be hazardous.

sec14-card-sec14-R16.front: What two route or schedule choices does the handbook recommend for poor night vision?
sec14-card-sec14-R16.expected_back: The poor-night-vision guidance favors slower travel on well-lit streets or limiting driving to daylight.

sec14-card-sec14-R17.front: Where should you aim your gaze when oncoming headlights dazzle eyes with slow glare recovery?
