sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Classic vehicles originally manufactured without safety belt anchors cannot mount modern restraints and are exempted by statute.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Which model years mark the factory-beltless exemption for passenger cars versus vans and trucks?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Memorize both vintage cutoffs separately because passenger cars before nineteen sixty-seven differ from vans or trucks before nineteen seventy-two.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: How do child-restraint requirements apply to emergency and law-enforcement vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Urgent response transport cannot wait for custom car-seat installation, so police and emergency units are excluded from the mandate.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: Which buses carrying children are included on the child-restraint exemption list?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: High-backed compartmentalized seating on buses built for student or youth-group trips places those carriers on the statutory exemption list.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: When are public-transportation buses or other transit vehicles exempt from child-restraint rules?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: City and regional transit fleets manufactured without passenger seat belts qualify for the public-transportation exemption.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: How does the child-restraint law treat a driver giving emergency aid or assistance to a child or parent?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Helping a stranded or injured child, parent, or guardian in an urgent situation does not trigger a child-seat citation.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: Above what weight does handbook booster guidance start, and what else must you check?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Crossing forty pounds is only the starting benchmark because every booster model sets its own exact height and weight caps.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: Which booster style fits a seat with a headrest, and where should that headrest sit?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: With a vehicle headrest adjusted behind the ears at mid-head height, a backless booster positions belts while preventing whiplash.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: Which booster type does the handbook recommend when the vehicle seat has no headrest?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Without a built-in head restraint behind the child, a high-back booster supplies essential head and neck support in rear impacts.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: Which belt type works with a belt-positioning booster, and what if a seat only has a lap belt?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Belt-positioning boosters depend on an upper strap to hold the torso, so a lap-only seat requires choosing another option.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: Where must a child's back and buttocks stay for a vehicle seat belt to fit properly?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Slouching forward to bend the legs pulls the lap strap onto the soft belly where crash forces cause severe harm.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: Where must both the shoulder strap and lap strap sit for proper seat-belt fit on a child?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Keeping the upper strap centered on shoulder and chest while the lower strap hugs hips or upper thighs routes crash loads onto bone.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: How must a child's knees line up with the vehicle seat cushion to pass the belt-fit check?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: When legs are too short to bend naturally at the cushion edge, kids slide forward and ruin safe lap-belt placement.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: Where must a child's feet rest, and how long must they maintain that belt-fit posture?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Fitting properly for ten seconds in the driveway is not enough if dangling legs make the child squirm mid-drive.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: When is a vehicle occupant medically exempt from wearing a safety belt?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Only a physician's written statement explaining that physical or medical reasons make belt wear inadvisable excuses an unbuckled occupant.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: How does the belt law apply in a passenger vehicle that federal rules did not require to have belts?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Occupants riding in vintage passenger cars built before federal belt equipment mandates are excused from wearing nonexistent straps.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: When is a United States Postal Service worker exempt from the safety-belt requirement?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Frequent curbside mailbox stops excuse postal workers only while actively performing carrier delivery duties, not off-duty errands.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: Does someone properly strapped into a child safety-restraint system also need a separate adult belt?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: An approved child seat already anchors the rider safely, so the law does not demand a second separate belt over them.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.question_text: When is a front-seat occupant exempt from wearing a safety belt due to seating capacity?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.teaching_text: If every working belt in the vehicle is already buckled around other riders, the remaining front-seat occupant is legally exempt.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: How does the Wyoming handbook describe the Driver License Compact?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Member states share conviction reports so drivers cannot dodge serious traffic penalties simply by crossing state lines.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: What two-part concept anchors the handbook's Driver License Compact discussion?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Holding only one license tied to one nationwide history prevents drivers from hiding suspensions behind multiple state cards.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: What do you automatically consent to under Implied Consent by driving on a public street or highway?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Using public roads carries built-in agreement to take blood-alcohol chemical tests if an officer arrests you for impaired driving.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: What can law enforcement do if an arrested driver refuses a required chemical test?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Saying no at the roadside does not block evidence gathering because police can secure a warrant for an approved tester.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: What happens when a required test shows blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero eight percent or higher?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Hitting zero point zero eight percent triggers a ninety-day license suspension right away alongside potential criminal court punishments.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: At what lower blood alcohol concentration can an impaired-driving conviction still happen with supporting evidence?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Staying under zero point zero eight will not save you if sloppy driving and zero point zero five prove impairment.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: What simple step does the handbook recommend to keep from driving after drinking?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Waiting until alcohol clouds your judgment makes bad choices likely, so arrange your sober ride before taking a sip.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: How does alcohol affect activity inside the brain and spinal cord?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Because alcohol is a central nervous system depressant rather than a stimulant, nerve signals needed for steering and braking lag.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: Where does alcohol absorbed from the stomach go next?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Unlike solid food that requires full digestion, alcohol passes directly from the stomach into circulating blood and hits brain tissue.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What happens to blood-alcohol level and impairment as larger amounts of alcohol are consumed?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Every added drink pushes blood-alcohol concentration higher and deepens the mental and physical breakdown behind the wheel.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: What does the term Blood Alcohol Concentration measure?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Testing blood alcohol concentration measures actual alcohol circulating in your bloodstream rather than counting how many glasses you held.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: How does the total quantity of alcohol consumed relate to blood alcohol concentration?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Putting more pure alcohol into your system directly raises the concentration your liver has to clear over time.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: How does the length of time spent drinking relate to blood alcohol concentration?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Downing drinks rapidly outpaces your body's steady elimination rate and spikes blood alcohol higher than spacing them apart.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: How does a person's body weight relate to blood alcohol concentration?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Two friends finishing identical drinks in the same hour can reach very different levels when their body weights differ.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: How does the handbook describe the look and taste of pure ethyl alcohol?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Sweet flavors and dark colors come from mixers or brewing ingredients, hiding pure ethyl alcohol's clear look and burning taste.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: How easily does ethyl alcohol blend with other liquids, and what does adding water or mixer do?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Adding soda or water dilutes drink strength per sip, though total pure alcohol inside the glass stays unchanged.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: About what percentage of alcohol does beer usually contain according to the handbook?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Lower percentage per ounce tricks drivers into thinking beer is harmless even though larger cans deliver a full dose.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: What alcohol percentages does the handbook list in its wine examples?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Table and fortified wines pack twelve or twenty percent alcohol, concentrating far more ethyl alcohol per ounce than beer.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: About what percentage range of alcohol does the handbook give for hard-liquor examples?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: At roughly forty to fifty percent alcohol, even a small shot glass carries as much punch as a full beer.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: Which beer, wine, and eighty-six-proof liquor serving sizes each contain about half an ounce of alcohol?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Twelve ounces of beer, three to five ounces of wine, and one-and-a-half ounces of eighty-six-proof liquor deliver equal half-ounce alcohol.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: How soon can someone begin noticing the effects of alcohol?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Rapid absorption from the stomach means subtle changes in mood and reaction begin shortly after the first drink starts.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: Why can alcohol impairment keep intensifying even after you put your glass down?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Alcohol still sitting in your stomach continues entering your bloodstream during the drive home, making impairment worse mid-trip.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: What effect does having food or milk in the stomach have on alcohol?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Eating beforehand slows how quickly alcohol enters the blood, though it never stops absorbed alcohol from impairing your brain.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: Can coffee, a cold shower, or exercise clear alcohol faster to sober you up sooner?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Caffeine and cold water only create a wide-awake impaired driver while your liver still clears alcohol at its fixed pace.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: Why will a heavier person likely show a lower blood alcohol concentration than a lighter person from equal drinks?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Greater blood and body-fluid volume dilutes the same dose across a larger person, leaving lighter drivers higher faster.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: Is someone at zero point zero eight percent impaired if they show zero outward signs of drunkenness?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Looking steady in the mirror fools drivers because mental and physical driving skills are already degraded at point zero eight.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: Why can outward behavior mislead you when judging whether a regular drinker is safe to drive?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Practiced drinkers may walk and talk smoothly at high blood alcohol levels while their crash-avoidance reactions remain dangerously slow.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: What happens to traffic judgment and decision accuracy as blood alcohol rises, regardless of outward appearance?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Whether someone slurs or acts completely normal, climbing blood alcohol steadily erodes accurate hazard judgment in real traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: Which four core mental-and-physical driving steps does alcohol weaken?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Safe driving relies on spotting hazards, forecasting moves, choosing action, and steering cleanly, and alcohol degrades all four steps.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: Which three dulled senses lower an impaired driver's ability to detect traffic hazards?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Spotting trouble early takes sharp eyes, clear ears, and balanced feel for car motion, all blunted by alcohol.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: How can an alcohol-impaired driver's visual scanning fail when looking down the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Locking your gaze onto taillights or lane lines blinds you to pedestrians, cross traffic, and changing signals nearby.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: What does the handbook warn alcohol impairment can do to peripheral detection?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Severe tunnel vision can almost erase awareness of pedestrians stepping off curbs or cars merging beside your fenders.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: Alongside reduced hearing, what visual judgment skill does alcohol weaken?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Misjudging how far away oncoming headlights are while missing horn or siren cues sets up intersection and passing crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: What lane-keeping mistakes happen when a high-alcohol driver loses body-position awareness?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Without inner-ear and muscle feedback, impaired drivers weave over centerlines, straddle lane dividers, or wander off pavement.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: How do impaired vision, hearing, and body-position sensing affect the predict step?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: When sensory inputs arrive late or distorted, you cannot anticipate a merging car or sudden brake tap ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: What happens in critical driving moments when senses, judgments, and predictions are faulty?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Split-second emergencies punish bad inputs because flawed perception and guesswork lead straight to the wrong evasive choice.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: What dangerous mindset pair can alcohol create that leads to bad driving choices?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Feeling bolder right as your skills drop tempts impaired drivers to speed, tailgate, and gamble on tight gaps.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: What errors did drink-impaired simulator subjects make despite looking sober?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Even subjects who seemed outwardly fine steered the wrong way or stomped the accelerator instead of braking under pressure.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: Even if a drink-impaired driver picks the right evasive move, what still goes wrong?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Sluggish nerve-to-muscle signaling delays turning the wheel or pressing the pedal long enough to turn near-misses into crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour, how much farther did the handbook's drinking driver roll before touching the brakes?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.teaching_text: Rolling at least two extra car lengths before your foot even hits the brake pedal erases your stopping margin.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.question_text: How much extra delay time produced that braking lag, and does it matter at slower speeds?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.teaching_text: Adding just two-fifths of a second to reaction time can mean striking a child in a neighborhood street too.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.question_text: How does alcohol affect inexperienced drivers compared with seasoned drivers?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.teaching_text: Beginners still need full conscious focus for basic car control, so even small amounts of alcohol multiply mistakes sharply.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.question_text: How do beginning drinkers compare with experienced drinkers after consuming alcohol?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.teaching_text: Unfamiliarity with alcohol's effects hits novice drinkers harder, compounding the danger when paired with limited driving experience.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.question_text: What happens when unusual weather, lighting, or road conditions combine with alcohol?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.teaching_text: Glare, storms, and unfamiliar curves demand sharper concentration at the exact moment alcohol strips away your coping skills.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.question_text: Which physical or emotional states can already impair you before alcohol strips away compensation?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.teaching_text: Tiredness, anger, anxiety, upset, or even intense excitement already distracts you before alcohol removes your self-check.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.question_text: Which specific emotion does the handbook single out as particularly dangerous when mixed with alcohol?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.teaching_text: Hot temper paired with lowered inhibition fuels aggressive speeding and reckless confrontations behind the wheel.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: Which four common medication types can disrupt your ability to identify, predict, decide, or execute?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Everyday medicine-cabinet drugs can blunt scanning, judgment, and steering reflexes just as dangerously as alcohol.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What risky mental state can diet pills and stay-awake pills create?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Feeling artificially wired tricks tired drivers into misjudging their skill and taking aggressive chances in traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: What critical driving skills do stay-awake drugs fail to restore while hiding fatigue?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Stimulants mask yawns without bringing back fast hazard detection or crisp split-second decision-making when exhaustion sets in.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: How can sleeping pills affect your alertness, thinking, and emotions?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Residual sedatives dull concentration and emotional steadiness, leaving you groggy and erratic in traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: How long can sleeping pills continue impairing driving decision tasks?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: A pill taken late at night can still slow morning commute choices for several hours after waking up.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: Which four ingredients in allergy or cold remedies can cause drowsiness or foggy thinking?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Over-the-counter syrups and tablets often pack sedating ingredients that make you nod off behind the wheel.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.question_text: How do tranquilizers affect a driver's mind, alertness, and physical responses?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.teaching_text: Calming medications depress attention, emotional balance, clear thinking, and brake-pedal speed all at once.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.question_text: How long may the impairing effects of tranquilizers last?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.teaching_text: Feeling calmer right after taking a dose does not mean the multi-hour reaction slowdown has worn off.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.question_text: Why are the overall effects of mind-altering street drugs unpredictable?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.teaching_text: Unregulated batches swing wildly in potency and contaminants, making impairment severity impossible to predict before driving.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.question_text: Which mental, visual, and spatial skills can mind-altering drugs disrupt?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.teaching_text: Distorted time and distance perception ruins safe gap judgment at intersections and highway merges.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.question_text: What is the rule for someone under the influence of mind-altering drugs?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.teaching_text: No defensive-driving trick compensates for warped perception, so staying completely out of the driver's seat is mandatory.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.question_text: When is it safe to drive after starting a brand-new medication?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.teaching_text: Wait to see how your body reacts off the road before trusting a new medication in live traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.question_text: What legal consequence can result from driving under the influence of a controlled drug?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.teaching_text: Impaired-driving laws punish drug impairment just like alcohol, carrying full arrest and conviction consequences.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.question_text: What should you ask your doctor whenever a medication is prescribed?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.teaching_text: A quick question at the clinic flags drowsiness, dizziness, or blurred vision before you commute home.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.question_text: What should you do before buying or taking any nonprescription drug?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.teaching_text: Store-bought boxes print drowsiness and operating-machinery warnings on the label so you can choose a non-drowsy option.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.question_text: What three main enforcement or safety reasons can prompt an officer to initiate a traffic stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.teaching_text: Flashing lights might flag a loose load or road hazard, address a moving violation, or check a vehicle description.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.question_text: Which two non-offense situations might also cause an officer to stop a motorist?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.teaching_text: Officers sometimes pull drivers over simply to render roadside help or gather witness details right after an incident.

sec06-card-sec06-R23.question_text: How should you respond when police lights or a siren signal you to stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R23.teaching_text: Smooth braking and pulling to a safe spot on the right tells the officer immediately that you are cooperating.

sec06-card-sec06-R24.question_text: Which three roadside locations should you avoid halting in during a traffic stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R24.teaching_text: Stopping in active lanes, narrow bridges, or pinned against guardrails leaves nowhere safe for the officer to stand.

sec06-card-sec06-R25.question_text: What gear action should you take right after bringing your vehicle to a stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R25.teaching_text: Shifting into park prevents an accidental roll if your foot slips and signals that you are staying put.

sec06-card-sec06-R26.question_text: Which three cab actions prepare you to communicate clearly during a traffic stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R26.teaching_text: Lowering your window, ending phone calls, and turning down music lets both sides hear instructions clearly without tension.

sec06-card-sec06-R27.question_text: Should you step out of your vehicle during a traffic stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R27.teaching_text: Popping your door open unannounced looks threatening and puts you near passing traffic, so wait for instructions.

sec06-card-sec06-R28.question_text: Where should you keep your hands as the officer approaches and speaks with you?
sec06-card-sec06-R28.teaching_text: Resting both hands openly on the wheel reassures the approaching officer that you are not reaching for anything hidden.

sec06-card-sec06-R29.question_text: What will an officer generally share during a stop, while noting situations vary?
sec06-card-sec06-R29.teaching_text: Expect the officer to explain why you were stopped and give a name if asked, though urgent scenes vary.

sec06-card-sec06-R30.question_text: How should you inform an officer if there are weapons inside the vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R30.teaching_text: Calmly stating where a weapon sits while keeping your hands still prevents a dangerous misunderstanding.

sec06-card-sec06-R31.question_text: Which movements inside the cab should you avoid during a police stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R31.teaching_text: Quick reaches toward floorboards, back seats, or the passenger side look like hiding contraband or grabbing a weapon.
sec06-card-sec06-R31.must_match_memory_hook: No sudden floor, rear, side lunges

visual_sync.text_span: No sudden floor, rear, side lunges

sec06-card-sec06-R32.question_text: What extra lighting step should you take when stopped by police at night?
sec06-card-sec06-R32.teaching_text: Illuminating the cabin at night helps the officer see your hands clearly and keeps the encounter calm.

sec06-card-sec06-R33.question_text: Which three documents must you carry and present when requested by an officer?
sec06-card-sec06-R33.teaching_text: Keeping your driver license, insurance card, and registration together avoids frantic digging during a roadside check.

sec06-card-sec06-R34.question_text: What should you do before reaching for documents stored in a glove box or bag?
sec06-card-sec06-R34.teaching_text: Explaining where your registration sits before moving your hands keeps a routine paperwork grab completely predictable.

sec06-card-sec06-R35.question_text: What behavior should you encourage from passengers during a traffic stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R35.teaching_text: Chatter or movement from passengers distracts the officer and escalates tension during a roadside stop.

sec06-card-sec06-R36.question_text: Who does the handbook hold responsible for the vehicle and everyone riding in it?
sec06-card-sec06-R36.teaching_text: As the driver, you set the tone and carry responsibility for both vehicle condition and passenger conduct.

sec06-card-sec06-R37.question_text: How should you answer questions asked by the officer during a stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R37.teaching_text: Giving false details turns a simple roadside warning or traffic ticket into a far more serious legal problem.

sec06-card-sec06-R38.question_text: What should you do if you do not understand why you received a ticket?
sec06-card-sec06-R38.teaching_text: A calm, respectful question gets clear clarification on the spot without turning the stop confrontational.

sec06-card-sec06-R39.question_text: Why should you skip arguing a violation on the roadside, and where do disputes belong?
sec06-card-sec06-R39.teaching_text: Roadside debates never erase a written citation and only raise tension when the courtroom is built for contesting charges.
sec06-card-sec06-R39.must_match_memory_hook: Never argue roadside, contest in court

visual_sync.text_span: Never argue roadside, contest in court

sec06-card-sec06-R40.question_text: Can you refuse consent to a vehicle search, and when may an officer search anyway?
sec06-card-sec06-R40.teaching_text: You may decline voluntary consent respectfully, yet legal probable cause still authorizes an officer to search without permission.

sec06-card-sec06-R41.question_text: What must you do on an interstate when passing a stopped emergency or maintenance vehicle with flashing lights?
sec06-card-sec06-R41.teaching_text: Putting an entire empty buffer lane between highway traffic and roadside responders prevents deadly shoulder strikes.

sec06-card-sec06-R42.question_text: How much must you cut speed on a two-lane road past a lighted emergency or maintenance vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R42.teaching_text: When no extra lane exists to move over, dropping at least twenty miles per hour protects workers steps away.

sec06-card-sec06-R43.question_text: What must you do when an emergency vehicle with activated lights overtakes you?
sec06-card-sec06-R43.teaching_text: Clearing toward the right curb and coming to a full stop opens an unobstructed lane until responders pass.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: When does the handbook's default speed-limit list apply, and what overrides it?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Statutory speed defaults only govern unmarked stretches because a posted speed-limit sign always sets the legal cap there.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: Which two interstate speed limits does the Wyoming handbook list without tying them to specific routes?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Watch roadside speed signs on Wyoming interstates because corridors alternate between seventy-five and eighty miles per hour.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: What is the listed speed limit on a Wyoming secondary highway unless posted otherwise?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Unmarked two-lane state highways top out at seventy miles per hour rather than interstate speeds.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: What is the default speed limit in a residential area when signs do not state another speed?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Driveways, parked cars, and children playing near curbs require holding neighborhood speed to thirty miles per hour.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: What speed limit applies in a business area unless a different limit is posted?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Crosswalk foot traffic and frequent storefront turns make thirty miles per hour the safe unposted cap downtown.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: What is the listed speed limit in a school zone unless signs specify another speed?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Young students darting toward crosswalks need short stopping distances that only twenty miles per hour provides.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: Why do roadway surface conditions affect your car's grip so strongly?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Every steering, braking, and acceleration force travels through rubber meeting pavement, so slick surfaces cut control immediately.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: How big is each tire's actual contact patch on the pavement according to the handbook?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Realizing four hand-sized patches hold thousands of pounds of moving metal explains why worn tread turns deadly.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: What should guide the driving speed you select at any moment?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Legal maximums assume ideal dry daylight, so gravel, rain, or glare demands dialing speed down to match conditions.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: When should you slow down for a curve, and what happens if you carry too much speed?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Braking hard mid-curve overloads front tires when excessive entry speed is already pushing them toward breaking traction.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: What is the maximum speed when approaching a blind intersection blocked by trees, shrubs, or buildings?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Creeping up at fifteen miles per hour or less gives you room to stop if hidden cross traffic appears.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: How does slippery pavement change tire traction and required speed compared with dry asphalt?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Reduced friction stretches stopping distance dramatically unless you trim your cruising speed below dry-road habits.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: By how much does the handbook say to reduce speed on a wet roadway?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Trimming five to ten off your dry-road pace helps tire grooves channel rainwater instead of hydroplaning.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: How much should you cut your speed when driving on packed snow?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Packed snow slashes tire traction so severely that cruising above half of normal speed outruns your brakes.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: How slow should you travel on ice, especially when other vehicles are ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Near-zero friction on ice calls for creeping at a crawl, and even slower when traffic sits ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: Why does driving faster than surrounding traffic raise your crash risk?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Weaving past slower cars multiplies lane changes, blind-spot conflicts, and closing-speed errors every mile.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: How risky is driving well below traffic speed or stopping without warning?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Rolling roadblocks and surprise stops trigger chain-reaction rear-end collisions from drivers closing fast behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: How should you respond when you spot a slower vehicle ahead in your lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Easing off the gas early avoids last-second brake slams that catch trailing drivers off guard.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: What legal road right do bicyclists hold, and how must drivers adjust?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Because cyclists share full legal access to public roadways, impatient crowding or buzzing past at full speed is unlawful.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: How fast may you safely travel at night relative to your headlights?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Outdriving your headlights means any stalled vehicle or deer appearing at beam's edge is already inside your stopping zone.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: About how many feet of clear headlight visibility does the handbook's nighttime example assume?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Remembering the two-hundred-fifty-foot beam reach anchors why open-highway daytime speeds outrun night sightlines.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: In that two-hundred-fifty-foot headlight example, what happens above fifty-five miles per hour?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Pushing past fifty-five miles per hour stretches total stopping distance beyond the two hundred fifty feet your beams light up.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: How short can forward visibility drop in very heavy rain, a snowstorm, or thick fog?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Downpours, whiteouts, and dense fog can shrink forward sight to one hundred feet or less within seconds.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: What driving speed is safe when storms or fog cut forward sight to one hundred feet or less?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: When you cannot see past one hundred feet in blinding weather, moving down the highway at any speed gambles blindly.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: What should you do when weather makes forward visibility inadequate for safe driving?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Getting completely off active lanes and waiting out blinding weather beats creeping down the highway into a pileup.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: What do right-of-way laws actually specify when paths cross?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Notice the wording trap on exams because statutes never grant absolute priority and instead name who must yield.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: How should you respond when another driver fails to yield the right of way?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Being legally right never softens metal impact, so yield your turn anytime someone barges into your path.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: How does traffic law classify bicycles regarding operator rights and duties?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Treating bicycles as vehicles means riders follow traffic controls and earn the same intersection yielding rules as cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: Who must you yield to at an unmarked intersection without signs or signals, even if you arrived first?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Watch Wyoming's strict twist at uncontrolled crossings where the vehicle on your right goes even if you got there first.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: Why must you scan both sides whenever paths cross instead of trusting signs or lights alone?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Green bulbs and stop signs cannot physically halt a distracted red-light runner barreling across your lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: What exact sequence of head checks does the handbook describe for scanning an intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Looking straight ahead, sweeping left then right, and rechecking both ways catches fast movers before you commit.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: Why should your side scan check to the left early at an intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Cross traffic coming from your left occupies the very first lane your front bumper enters.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: When should you check cross traffic as you approach a yield-controlled intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Scanning early lets you adjust speed smoothly or stop cleanly at the line instead of braking late in cross traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: Which cross-traffic vehicles must you yield to when a yield sign governs your lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Any cross vehicle close enough that pulling out forces them to brake or swerve has priority over your entry.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: Who must you yield to when turning onto a street or highway?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Entering an active roadway from a turn requires waiting until oncoming or cross vehicles are safely clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: What three steps complete a smooth entry into moving traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Picking an open gap, steering cleanly in, and accelerating to traffic pace prevents rear-end conflicts behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-R22.question_text: Who gets to go first at a four-way stop?
sec07-card-sec07-R22.teaching_text: Watching arrival order as you roll up keeps four-way intersections moving smoothly one vehicle at a time.

sec07-card-sec07-R23.question_text: Who should you yield to when arrival order is uncertain at a four-way stop?
sec07-card-sec07-R23.teaching_text: Letting the driver on your right proceed breaks simultaneous-arrival ties cleanly without hesitation waves.

sec07-card-sec07-R24.question_text: What is the rule on insisting on your turn when another driver pushes ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-R24.teaching_text: Giving up three seconds of priority beats trading paint with an aggressive or confused driver.

sec07-card-sec07-R25.question_text: What happens to your right of way if you enter an intersection above the legal speed?
sec07-card-sec07-R25.teaching_text: Drivers breaking the speed law into an intersection lose every legal right-of-way claim they otherwise had.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: How quickly can winter storms change pavement conditions on Wyoming highways?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: High-elevation wind and snow squalls can glaze dry Wyoming asphalt with sheet ice in minutes.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: When and how fast should you test road-surface traction in winter conditions?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Checking pavement grip only at low speed with zero trailing cars keeps a test slip from causing a collision.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: How does the handbook suggest using the brake pedal to gauge a winter road surface?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Gently touching the pedal reveals whether tires bite and slow down or start sliding sideways on hidden ice.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: Which three road spots can stay icy even after sunshine clears open pavement?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Cold air circulating under bridge decks and tree or canyon shade keeps hidden ice patches frozen all afternoon.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: Because black ice blends into asphalt, what surface shift must you watch for?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Glare black ice looks just like harmless wet pavement until tire spray vanishes and steering goes light.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Why is thawing ice covered by a thin film of water especially treacherous?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Meltwater acts like liquid grease atop solid ice, cutting traction far below colder dry snow.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: How should you use the gas pedal and front wheels when starting from a stop on snow or ice?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Pointing tires straight ahead and feeding throttle smoothly prevents wheelspin before rolling forward.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: Can four-wheel-drive and front-wheel-drive vehicles still skid despite better starting traction?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Extra driven wheels help you get rolling, yet sudden throttle or gear jolts still break tire grip on ice.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: What gas-pedal mistake does the handbook name as a power change that can trigger a winter skid?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Abruptly dumping the accelerator creates sudden engine-braking drag on driven tires and breaks icy traction.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: What extra danger faces a four-wheel-drive vehicle with a high center of gravity during a skid?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Tall trucks and sport-utility vehicles trip and roll much more easily if a sideways slide catches dry pavement or snowbanks.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: Which vehicle types need extra following distance in winter conditions?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Four-wheel drive never improves four-wheel braking on ice, so every vehicle needs a bigger winter buffer.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.question_text: How does the handbook's winter landmark count test whether you are following too closely?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.teaching_text: Reaching the sign or post before finishing a four-count behind the car ahead proves your winter cushion is too short.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.question_text: Why must you know whether your vehicle uses conventional brakes or anti-lock brakes?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.teaching_text: Using the wrong foot motion in a slick emergency stop wastes precious grip right when you need control.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.question_text: What happens if you jam down hard on conventional non-anti-lock brakes?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.teaching_text: Sliding locked tires cannot steer around obstacles and slide straight ahead out of control.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.question_text: How fast should you pump conventional brakes according to the handbook?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.teaching_text: Rhythmic once-per-second pumping lets non-anti-lock wheels keep rolling enough to maintain steering control.

sec07-card-sec07-R16.question_text: Why must you never pump anti-lock brakes during a hard stop?
sec07-card-sec07-R16.teaching_text: Letting up defeats the computer sensors that already pulse brake pressure automatically faster than any human foot.

sec07-card-sec07-R17.question_text: What simple habit makes stopping easier and cuts skid risk on slick pavement?
sec07-card-sec07-R17.teaching_text: Starting from a slower pace asks far less friction from your tires than trying to rescue a fast slide.

sec07-card-sec07-R18.question_text: How should you steer and use the gas pedal if your vehicle begins skidding?
sec07-card-sec07-R18.teaching_text: Smooth steering into the slide paired with easing off the throttle lets rolling tires recapture directional grip.
sec07-card-sec07-R18.must_match_memory_hook: Turn gently into skid, ease gas

visual_sync.text_span: Turn gently into skid, ease gas

sec07-card-sec07-R19.question_text: How should you handle speed, steering, and braking in a ground blizzard?
sec07-card-sec07-R19.teaching_text: Blowing ground snow hides ice ruts and lane edges, so every steering and pedal input must stay slow and gentle.

sec07-card-sec07-R20.question_text: What should you do if a vehicle ahead spins out on an icy hill?
sec07-card-sec07-R20.teaching_text: Trying to weave around a spun-out car on sheet ice usually traps your vehicle sideways across the grade too.

sec07-card-sec07-R21.question_text: Where should you park and what must you stay ready to do when helping at an icy crash scene?
sec07-card-sec07-R21.teaching_text: The exact slick patch that sent the first car sliding often sends approaching vehicles skidding into the same spot.
sec07-card-sec07-R21.must_match_memory_hook: Park far, stay ready to dodge

visual_sync.text_span: Park far, stay ready to dodge

sec07-card-sec07-R26.question_text: At what pace and in which circular direction does traffic move inside a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R26.teaching_text: Low speeds and one-way counterclockwise flow eliminate high-speed head-on and T-bone conflict angles.

sec07-card-sec07-R27.question_text: When is roundabout traffic supposed to yield rather than keep moving?
sec07-card-sec07-R27.teaching_text: Roundabouts stay fluid by flowing continuously except when yielding to circulating vehicles or pedestrians in crosswalks.

sec07-card-sec07-R28.question_text: How should you approach a roundabout, and who gets priority before you enter?
sec07-card-sec07-R28.teaching_text: Slowing on approach lets you yield first to crosswalk pedestrians and then to vehicles already circling.

sec07-card-sec07-R29.question_text: Which way do you look for a safe gap before merging into a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R29.teaching_text: Because circulating cars travel counterclockwise, every approaching conflict vehicle comes toward you from your left.

sec07-card-sec07-R30.question_text: Once circulating inside a roundabout, should you stop or keep moving unless yielding is required?
sec07-card-sec07-R30.teaching_text: Stopping mid-circle surprises trailing drivers who expect continuous movement until an exit crosswalk requires yielding.

sec07-card-sec07-R31.question_text: What two steps must you take as you leave a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R31.teaching_text: Flashing your right turn signal alerts waiting drivers while checking the exit crosswalk protects people on foot.

sec07-card-sec07-R32.question_text: Where should pedestrians cross when navigating a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R32.teaching_text: Cutting across the central island puts walkers inside curved lanes where drivers are scanning for gaps.

sec07-card-sec07-R33.question_text: What operational feature explains why roundabouts see fewer crashes, delays, and backups?
sec07-card-sec07-R33.teaching_text: Replacing red-light queues with steady low-speed merging cuts severe collisions and intersection wait time.

sec07-card-sec07-R34.question_text: What environmental and cost benefit comes from fewer stops and starts at roundabouts?
sec07-card-sec07-R34.teaching_text: Eliminating long red-light idling and repeated full-throttle launches saves gas and trims tailpipe exhaust.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: Where should you stop your vehicle to let an approaching emergency vehicle pass?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Pulling as close as practicable to the right edge or curb opens maximum center-road clearance for fast responders.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: Where must you avoid stopping while yielding to an emergency vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Freezing inside the intersection box blocks turning ambulances and fire trucks from clearing any cross street.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: How long must you remain stopped at the curb for an emergency vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Rolling back into traffic early cuts off fast-moving responders or trailing support units.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: Why should you keep your foot pressed on the brake while yielded for an emergency vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Glowing brake lamps give the approaching siren driver instant visual proof that your car will not roll out.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: What must you check for before pulling back into traffic after an emergency vehicle passes?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Police cruisers, fire engines, and ambulances often respond in pairs, and the first siren masks the second.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: What should you do if an emergency vehicle approaches before you enter a roundabout?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Stopping on the approach road keeps narrow curved roundabout aprons completely open for large fire apparatus.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: What is the rule if you are already circulating in a roundabout when an emergency vehicle approaches?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Halting mid-circle jams the curved lane, so finish to your exit and pull right once clear.
sec08-card-sec08-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Exit circle first, then pull right

visual_sync.text_span: Exit circle first, then pull right

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: Unless police direct otherwise, what must you do on a multi-lane highway near parked flashing work or emergency vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Moving to the farthest lane shields police, utility, municipal, and highway crews working feet from fast traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: How slow must you drop on a road with one lane each way when passing a parked emergency vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: When you cannot change lanes away from the shoulder, slowing at least twenty below the posted cap protects officers.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: Who carries responsibility for keeping pedestrian-and-vehicle traffic safe?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Safe crossings depend on alert motorists yielding cleanly and walkers following signals rather than stepping out blindly.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: When must you yield to a pedestrian in a marked crosswalk on your half of the road?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Whether an intersection has traffic lights or zero signals at all, a walker on your side gets priority.
sec08-card-sec08-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Yield whether signals exist or not

visual_sync.text_span: Yield whether signals exist or not

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: Who must you yield to when making a legal turn on red after a complete stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Drivers staring left for a gap in cars often miss a walker stepping lawfully into the near crosswalk.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: How do you recognize a blind pedestrian to whom you must always yield?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Never honk or inch around someone carrying a white cane or walking with a guide dog.
sec08-card-sec08-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Visible white cane or guide dog

visual_sync.text_span: Visible white cane or guide dog

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: At least how long does the handbook allow to spot a hazard, predict events, and choose a response?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Before your foot even moves toward a pedal, your brain burns at least a full second processing danger.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: About how long does it take to move your foot from the gas pedal to the brake?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Even an alert driver rolls farther down the highway during the three-quarters of a second before pads touch rotors.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: Which five factors determine your vehicle's physical braking distance?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: High entry speed, worn pads, bald tread, rough asphalt, or rain each stretches how far you roll under braking.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: How do a tractor-trailer's stopping time and distance compare with a passenger car at equal speed?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Cutting tightly in front of a heavy truck steals space its air brakes and cargo mass physically need.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: About how many feet does a passenger vehicle typically need to stop from fifty-five miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Nearly half a football field passes before a normal car halts from fifty-five miles per hour.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: In that fifty-five-mile-per-hour comparison, about how far does a heavy vehicle with a loaded trailer take to stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Loaded tractor-trailers roll roughly sixty feet farther than cars from the exact same highway cruising speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: How far can hot truck brakes stretch stopping distance in heavy traffic according to the handbook?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Stop-and-go braking heats heavy drum brakes until fade can double a rig's stopping run toward four hundred feet.
sec08-card-sec08-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Hot truck brakes reach four hundred

visual_sync.text_span: Hot truck brakes reach four hundred

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: How do fatigue, alcohol, or inattention hurt stopping performance before brakes ever engage?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Even brand-new tires cannot save you if drowsiness, drinks, or phone distraction delays spotting trouble ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: When must drivers in both directions stop for a school bus flashing red lights, and what exception applies?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Only a physical barrier or separate divided roadway excuses opposite-direction traffic from stopping for red bus lamps.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: Once stopped for a school bus, when may you start moving again?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Children may still be crossing near the bumper until the bus rolls forward or cancels its red flashers.
sec08-card-sec08-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Bus moves or red lights stop

visual_sync.text_span: Bus moves or red lights stop

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: How should you drive when a physical median legally lets you pass a red-light school bus?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Late-running students can still dart unexpectedly toward a bus across separated roadways.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: Where must your vehicle stop at a stop sign, steady red light, or flashing red light?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Rolling onto painted crosswalk bars forces pedestrians out into active cross traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: What must you do when pulling onto a street from a driveway, alley, building, or parking lot?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Sidewalk users and street traffic have priority over vehicles emerging from private drives, alleys, or garages.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: What does the handbook require when entering a business district from a side road?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Watch this Wyoming handbook rule because side roads feeding busy commercial blocks require stopping before entering.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: Why must you stop whenever a police officer directs you to, even at a green light?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Live traffic control by law enforcement always supersedes painted lines, posted signs, and overhead signal bulbs.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: What must you do when red lights flash or gates lower at a railroad crossing?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Trying to beat lowering gates misjudges fast closing train speed with catastrophic results.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: How must you respond when a flagger signals you to stop near tracks or a work zone?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Flaggers guard single-lane construction shifts and rail hazards you cannot yet see from your seat.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: What must you do when a blind person with a white cane or guide dog tries to cross?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Stopping fully protects pedestrians relying on sound cues rather than eye contact to cross safely.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: What is your immediate legal duty if you are involved in a traffic crash in any way?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Leaving any collision scene turns an accident into a serious hit-and-run offense.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: Which road configurations are covered in the handbook's school-bus stopping diagrams?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Exam diagrams contrast undivided two-lane or four-lane roads, where everyone stops, against physically divided highways.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: On a divided roadway, which traffic must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Students do not cross physical highway medians, so only lanes sharing the bus's roadway side must halt.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: Which mirrors must you check before starting a lane change?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Checking both center and outside glass shows closing speed behind you plus cars alongside your rear quarter.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: How do you clear your blind spot before moving into another lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Mirrors leave hidden zones beside your rear fenders that only a quick over-the-shoulder look reveals.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: On a multi-lane road, what conflict from neighboring lanes must you check before changing lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Two drivers converging into the same center lane from opposite sides sideswipe each other unless someone checks.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: When must you activate your turn signal for a lane change?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Flipping the lever only after your tires cross the lane stripes gives nearby drivers zero advance warning.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: Where near an intersection does the handbook prohibit changing lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Switching lanes right before or inside an intersection surprises turning and cross-street drivers.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: Which two lateral maneuvers always require using a signal?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Signaling both turns and lane shifts communicates every sideways move before your car leaves its path.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: At least how many feet before an intersection must you start signaling a turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: One hundred feet gives trailing and oncoming motorists time to adjust speed before you brake for the corner.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: At higher highway speeds, how many seconds ahead of a turn does the handbook recommend signaling?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Fast highway cars cover one hundred feet in barely a blink, so four to five seconds gives real notice.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: How should electrical turn signals match your intended maneuver?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Flashing the wrong blinker misleads waiting cross-street traffic into pulling straight into your path.
sec08-card-sec08-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Right for right, left for left

visual_sync.text_span: Right for right, left for left

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: Which arm is used to give manual hand signals from the driver's seat?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Extending your left arm out the driver window makes every hand position visible to traffic around you.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: How do you position your left arm and hand to signal a right turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Bending at the elbow with hand and forearm pointed straight skyward distinguishes a right turn from left or stop.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.question_text: How do you hold your left arm to give a hand signal for slowing or stopping?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.teaching_text: Pointing your left forearm and open hand downward from the elbow warns following drivers when brake lamps fail.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.question_text: When should you decide and prepare for an upcoming turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.teaching_text: Planning early prevents sudden swerves across lanes when you realize your street is right beside you.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.question_text: When and how should you position your vehicle in the proper turning lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.teaching_text: Using mirrors, signals, and blind-spot checks well ahead of the corner avoids cutting off through traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.question_text: What communication step precedes slowing into your planned turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.teaching_text: Alerting drivers and pedestrians which way you intend to turn prevents surprise conflicts at the corner.

sec08-card-sec08-R16.question_text: What two actions must you take right before turning into the cross street?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.teaching_text: Trimming speed while checking the crosswalk and target lane catches pedestrians, cyclists, or turning cars early.

sec08-card-sec08-R17.question_text: Where must your vehicle finish as you complete a turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.teaching_text: Swinging wide into an outer lane risks sideswiping cars turning legally beside you or oncoming traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.question_text: What should you do with your speed once you straighten out after a turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.teaching_text: Lingering at cornering speed after completing a turn creates a rear-end hazard for through traffic behind you.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.question_text: What physical check should you do before getting in to back your vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.teaching_text: Stepping behind the rear bumper spots small children, pets, or low toys hidden below trunk sightlines.

sec08-card-sec08-R20.question_text: Why are mirrors not enough while backing, and how should you look instead?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.teaching_text: Twisting your head and shoulders to look out the back glass eliminates huge mirror blind zones.

sec08-card-sec08-R21.question_text: Where should your steering hand sit and how fast should you move when backing?
sec08-card-sec08-R21.teaching_text: Anchoring one hand at top-center while creeping slowly keeps reverse steering responsive and controlled.

sec08-card-sec08-R22.question_text: What readiness mindset must you keep from start to finish while backing?
sec08-card-sec08-R22.teaching_text: Pedestrians and shopping-lot cars step behind reversing vehicles suddenly, so hover ready to halt immediately.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: Which two roadway traffic controls forbid you from overtaking another vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Engineers place no-passing signs and solid stripes where sightlines are too short to spot oncoming cars in time.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Which seven ahead-of-you people, vehicles, or road features require waiting rather than passing?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Crests, bends, bridges, crossings, and junctions hide oncoming traffic or turning cars until a head-on crash is unavoidable.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: How many vehicles may you attempt to overtake at once on a two-lane road?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Stringing multiple vehicles into one pass doubles your time in the oncoming lane and blocks your escape gap.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: May you follow right behind another driver who is already overtaking a vehicle ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: The lead passer blocks your view of oncoming headlights and may take the only open merge slot ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: When is the only time you may pass a school bus flashing its red lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Children cross unpredictably around stopped buses, so only a physical median barrier or separate roadway removes that crossing risk.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: What judgment should you make before even starting a passing maneuver?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Skipping an unnecessary pass eliminates head-on exposure when you are turning soon or traffic ahead is already bunched.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: How far behind the vehicle ahead should you begin your passing procedure?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Crowding the rear bumper blinds you to oncoming traffic and robs you of room to build passing speed safely.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: What two resources must you verify exist before pulling out to overtake?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Misjudging closing speed on open Wyoming highways turns a tight gap into a high-speed head-on emergency.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: What two steps must you take immediately before moving out to pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Another driver behind you may have already entered the left lane to overtake you first.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: Once your signals and all-around checks are done, how do you initiate the pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Building brisk momentum as you move left shortens the seconds spent exposed in opposing or adjacent lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: What mirror cue tells you it is safe to move back into the right lane after passing a car?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Waiting until the overtaken car's entire front appears in your center mirror prevents clipping its bumper as you merge.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: What must be true about the vehicle you are overtaking for Wyoming's passing-speed exception to apply?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: The exception exists to clear slow vehicles briskly on qualified roads, never to leapfrog traffic already at the limit.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: By how much may you exceed the posted limit under the handbook's qualifying passing-speed allowance?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Exceeding that ten-mile-per-hour ceiling turns a brief passing boost into a citable speeding violation.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: What is the baseline safety requirement before you ever pass another vehicle on the right?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Drivers expect overtakes on the left and check right-side mirrors far less consistently before drifting over.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: What maneuver by the vehicle ahead lets you pass on the right if it is safe to do so?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Even when a lead car signals left, confirm paved lane clearance so you never clip curb or oncoming turners.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: Is it legal to drive off the paved roadway to pass another vehicle on the right?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Gravel shoulders hide soft edges, culverts, and parked breakdowns that cause rollovers at road speed.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: What roadway and traffic setup also allows safe passing on the right?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Multilane one-way or divided corridors carry continuous streams where right-lane flow naturally moves past slower left-lane cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: Why does passing on the right carry extra collision danger?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Right-side blind zones are wider than left-side ones, so a driver shifting right can sideswipe you without warning.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: What lane condition must exist before you attempt to overtake a bicyclist?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Squeezing past a rider against oncoming traffic forces a deadly choice if either vehicle drifts inches.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: What must you do when there is not enough room to pass a bicyclist safely?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Matching the rider's speed behind them costs seconds while crowding past in a narrow lane risks a fatal sideswipe.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: What must you avoid doing while sharing a single traffic lane with a bicyclist?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Hovering next to a bike traps the rider with nowhere to swerve if wind, gravel, or a pothole appears.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: How should you adjust your speed while overtaking a bicyclist?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: High-speed mirror wash and air blast can destabilize a lightweight bicycle even without physical contact.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: How much lateral clearance should you keep between your vehicle and a bicyclist when space allows?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Three feet of side buffer absorbs normal pedaling wobble or a sudden dodge around road debris.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: What sudden vehicle movement must you watch for while driving past parked cars?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Curbside drivers often check mirrors poorly because adjacent parked vehicles block their view down the travel lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: What five visual clues warn you that a parked vehicle might be about to pull into traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Spotting tailpipe vapor, brake or reverse lamps, turn signals, angled tires, or a head inside buys early braking time.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: Who else might step or roll out unexpectedly from between parked vehicles?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Tall pickups and SUVs parked along the curb hide children, walkers, and cyclists until they enter your lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: Why is cutting back in close ahead of a passed truck and braking sharply so dangerous?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Loaded rigs need far longer stopping distance than cars, so stealing their front cushion invites a crushing rear-end hit.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: How should you manage your speed while overtaking a large commercial vehicle, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Hesitating or fluctuating pace stretches out a long pass and traps you beside massive trailer tires.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: What parts of a passed truck must show in your rearview mirror before you merge back ahead of it?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Seeing both headlamps and the full cab guarantees you have cleared the truck's deep front blind zone.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: How long can some double-trailer rigs be, and why must you factor that in before passing?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Passing a hundred-foot combination takes far more open road than overtaking a standard fifteen-foot sedan.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: Why do you need brisk, decisive speed when passing a large truck?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Cruising slowly alongside a trailer keeps your car invisible in the rig's side No-Zone for miles.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: How does lingering beside a truck endanger both you and the truck driver in an emergency?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: If debris or wind forces the rig to swerve, the driver cannot dodge without crushing a hidden car alongside.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: What two options do you have when approaching an emergency vehicle parked along the roadside?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: Responders working inches from live lanes need either an empty buffer lane or sharply reduced passing speeds.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: Why must you never tailgate directly behind a heavy vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Solid trailers have no center rearview mirror, making a tailgating sedan completely invisible to the cab.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: How does following a truck too closely hurt both the truck driver's sight and yours?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: The trailer wall hides your car from the trucker's mirrors while blocking every brake light and sign ahead of you.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: Besides a rear-end collision, what physical hazards threaten a car tailgating a heavy truck?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: Dual truck tires kick up rocks, winter ice chunks, and heavy tread strips before a close follower can dodge.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.question_text: What happens when a passenger car stays tucked in a large vehicle's side blind spot?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.teaching_text: Even wide-angle west-coast mirrors leave long side pockets where an entire compact car disappears from the cab.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.question_text: What can trigger a severe collision while you ride in a truck's side blind spot?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.teaching_text: When wind gusts, stalled shoulder cars, or merges force a quick rig lane change, unseen cars alongside get sideswiped.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.question_text: How does a right-turn squeeze crash happen beside a heavy vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.teaching_text: Long trailers swing wide left before tracking tight across the right curb, trapping any car beside them.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: Is it legal to park on the street side alongside another vehicle already stopped or parked at the curb?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Stopping in the live travel lane beside curb-parked cars chokes traffic flow and forces risky swerves into oncoming lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: Which three pedestrian or junction areas are off-limits for parking?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Vehicles parked on walkways or corners force walkers into live traffic and block intersection sight triangles.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: What does a yellow-painted curb near an intersection or driveway tell you about parking?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Yellow curb paint preserves turning radius and clear corner sightlines for drivers entering or exiting driveways and cross streets.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: Where must you avoid parking near a street-construction site?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Parking next to or across from active street work narrows narrowed lanes further and blocks heavy equipment access.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: Which two elevated or enclosed highway structures forbid parking?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Bridges and tunnels have zero shoulder escape room, turning any parked car into a bottleneck and rear-end trap.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: Which three posted sign restrictions make parking in a spot unlawful?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Official curb signs protect fire lanes, bus zones, and rush-hour corridors where even brief stops snarl traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: May you park in front of either a public or a private driveway?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Blocking any driveway traps residents inside and prevents emergency vehicles from pulling off the street.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: How many feet of clear space must you leave when parking near a fire hydrant?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Fire crews need fifteen unobstructed feet at the curb to hook heavy supply hoses without kinking lines.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: What must a vehicle display to park legally in a designated disabled parking space?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Accessible stalls and side aisles give wheelchair users essential ramp space near building entrances.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: How should you secure your brakes and front wheels when parking uphill next to a curb?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Angling front tires away from an uphill curb lets the back of the front tire catch the curb if brakes slip.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: Which way do you turn your front wheels in every hill-parking situation other than uphill with a curb?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Turning toward the curb or shoulder ensures a rolling car leaves the travel lane instead of drifting into traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: What three final steps should you complete before walking away from a car parked on a hill?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Shutting down, removing the key, and locking doors prevents theft and accidental gear shifts on steep grades.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.question_text: Where should all four tires sit when you make an emergency roadside stop, if space allows?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.teaching_text: Leaving even two tires on the travel lane invites distracted highway traffic to clip your rear corner.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.question_text: Which two road features must you avoid stopping on during a roadside emergency?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.teaching_text: Stopping on a crest or curve hides your disabled car until approaching drivers are too close to brake.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.question_text: Which vehicle lights must you activate whenever making an emergency roadside stop?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.teaching_text: Four-way hazard flashers alert approaching drivers from afar that your vehicle is stationary rather than moving.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.question_text: Which two smaller road users deserve extra attention before you pull out of a parking space?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.teaching_text: Slim profiles on bicycles and motorcycles easily hide behind door pillars and neighboring parked SUVs.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.question_text: What communication step is required before your car begins rolling out of a parking space?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.teaching_text: Signaling before the wheels move warns approaching drivers and cyclists not to squeeze past your bumper.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way when you are pulling out of a parking stall into traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.teaching_text: Through traffic and motorcycles already in the roadway have priority over any vehicle entering from the curb.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.question_text: How should you blend into a travel lane from a parking space?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.teaching_text: Darting abruptly off the curb startles through drivers and triggers panic braking or sideswipe crashes.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: How do you legally enter an interstate, and what ramp warning must you watch for?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Mistaking an off-ramp for an on-ramp puts you nose-to-nose with high-speed exiting vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Which two red-and-white regulatory signs warn that you are heading the wrong way onto a ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: DO NOT ENTER and WRONG WAY signs stand at ramp throats specifically to catch drivers before head-on freeway entry.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: What three steps must you take if you realize you are already driving the wrong way on a ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Getting onto the shoulder immediately clears the live ramp lane while you wait for a completely empty gap to turn around.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: What is the main purpose of an interstate acceleration lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Building up to highway pace before merging prevents high-speed through traffic from slamming on its brakes behind you.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: How should you locate an open space in interstate traffic before merging?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Side mirrors leave a wide blind pocket along the left rear quarter where fast right-lane cars hide.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: Once you pick a safe opening on the interstate, what two actions prepare your merge?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Timing your throttle to slide cleanly into the chosen pocket while signaling tells mainline drivers exactly where you are headed.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: When is the only situation you should stop while entering an interstate?
