sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Stopping unnecessarily at the end of an acceleration lane forces you to merge from zero miles per hour and invites rear-end hits.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: How fast should you be moving when you blend into interstate traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Entering much slower or faster than surrounding lanes creates instant closing-speed conflicts across multiple lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: Why must you keep watching the vehicle ahead of you on an entrance ramp instead of staring only at your mirror?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Looking back over your shoulder too long causes classic ramp rear-enders when a nervous lead driver panics and stops.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: Between vehicles already cruising on the interstate and vehicles entering from a ramp, who has priority?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Entering drivers must yield and fit into existing gaps rather than forcing freeway traffic to brake or swerve.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: What two assumptions must you never make about drivers already on the interstate as you merge?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Mainline traffic may be boxed in by left-lane passers or distracted, leaving gap selection entirely on you.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: How should you regulate your speed once settled into interstate travel?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Surging and slowing on high-speed highways triggers accordion braking waves while exceeding posted limits invites citations and crashes.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: What minimum following interval should you keep behind the vehicle ahead on the interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: At seventy-five miles per hour, you cover over a hundred feet every second before your foot even touches the brake.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: How should you adjust your interstate following interval during bad weather or on slick pavement?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Rain, snow, and black ice slash tire grip at highway speeds, multiplying the distance needed to stop straight.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: Which collision type does the Wyoming handbook name as the most common crash on interstates?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Tailgating at freeway speeds leaves zero margin when traffic ahead suddenly checks up for hazards or construction.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: How should you respond from the interstate when you spot vehicles coming down an entrance ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Shifting left opens a stress-free merge lane, provided you first verify no faster vehicle occupies your left blind spot.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: Which lane should you normally stay in on an interstate, and what habit should you avoid?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Weaving between lanes multiplies blind-spot conflicts while camping left blocks faster overtaking vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: What two steps are required before changing lanes on an interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Fast-closing interstate traffic enters mirror blind zones quickly, making both an early blinker and shoulder glance essential.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: When is it safe to pull back into the right lane after passing a vehicle on the interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Confirming the overtaken vehicle in your inside mirror keeps you from cutting across its front bumper at highway speed.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: What must you do if you accidentally pass your intended interstate exit?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Backing up on an interstate shoulder or ramp puts you in reverse against seventy-mile-per-hour traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: May a driver cut across an interstate median strip to turn around?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Crossing grassy or paved medians violates divided-highway law, risks getting stuck, and launches slow vehicles into fast left lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: What should you do as soon as you start feeling drowsy at the wheel?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Long rural stretches lull tired brains into microsleeps that cold air or loud music cannot reliably prevent.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: What action does the handbook advise when you become very sleepy on the highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: When heavy fatigue sets in, a quick leg stretch fails and only real off-highway sleep at a motel or rest stop restores alertness.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: How far ahead of your interstate exit should you signal and move into the exit-side lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Lining up a full mile early avoids last-second multi-lane dives across heavy trucks.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: When leaving an interstate, where should you begin slowing down?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Braking early in live through lanes surprises high-speed traffic behind you and causes rear-end collisions.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: What two adjustments must you make right after leaving an interstate for a surface road?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Highway velocitization makes forty miles per hour feel like a crawl while opposing traffic now shares an undivided road.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: Where should you position your vehicle during an interstate breakdown or emergency?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Parking deep onto the right shoulder puts maximum lateral buffer between your stalled car and fast traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: Why does the handbook allow rolling slowly on a flat tire for a short distance?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Ruining a tire rim costs far less than getting rear-ended on a shoulderless bridge or narrow underpass.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.question_text: Which lights must you turn on right away at an interstate emergency stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.teaching_text: Flashing hazard lamps warn approaching drivers early that your shoulder vehicle is stopped rather than merging.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.question_text: What extra roadside warning devices should you place during a nighttime interstate emergency stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.teaching_text: In rural darkness, flares or reflective triangles extend warning distance well behind a dim or dead battery.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.question_text: Which side of a disabled interstate vehicle must you never open a door on or step out from?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.teaching_text: High-speed mirror wash and drifting rigs can strike an open driver-side door or person in a split second.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.question_text: How do you signal that you need help after an interstate emergency stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.teaching_text: Universal visual distress cues let troopers spot your breakdown from afar while you wait safely out of traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.question_text: What must you do with passengers if a disabled vehicle cannot be moved off the interstate roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.teaching_text: A stalled car sitting in a live freeway lane is an impact magnet, so people must get well clear of the crash zone.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.question_text: How do standardized sign shapes help you in heavy weather or darkness?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.teaching_text: Snow, glare, or darkness can obscure lettering while an octagon, triangle, or diamond silhouette still tells you what to do.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.question_text: How do diamond-shaped signs differ in meaning from rectangular signs?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.teaching_text: Recognizing a hazard diamond versus a regulatory speed or direction rectangle prepares either caution or strict compliance.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: What core driving task do pavement markings help you accomplish?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Painted lane lines, turn arrows, and edge stripes keep vehicles aligned cleanly away from opposing and adjacent traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: What must you do when driving beneath an overhead lane arrow paired with the word ONLY?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Ignoring an ONLY lane control arrow creates sideswipe collisions with drivers lawfully turning beside you.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: How does a directional arrow painted on the asphalt compare in legal force to an overhead lane arrow?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Pavement arrows carry the exact same mandatory directional command as overhead signs, never just a suggestion.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: Where must you position your vehicle on a two-lane, two-way roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Staying strictly on the right half preserves clear oncoming separation especially around crests and curves.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: What general principle guides choosing your travel lane on a multilane road?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Cruising where traffic moves evenly reduces constant braking for curb turners and sudden lane shifts.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: When three or more lanes move in the same direction, which lane usually offers the smoothest flow?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Center lanes stay insulated from right-lane ramp merges and left-lane fast passers or left turners.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: Which three traffic movements belong in the left lane on a multilane road?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Keeping slower cruising out of the left lane prevents frustrated drivers from making risky right-side passes.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: Which two groups of drivers belong in the right-hand lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Grouping slower vehicles and upcoming right turns on the right keeps through lanes flowing predictably.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: When two lanes travel in the same direction without dedicated turn pockets, which lane usually flows smoothest?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: Without a center turn bay, cars stopping for left turns stall the left lane while right-lane traffic keeps moving.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: How do special left-turn lanes change which through lane may flow smoothest?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Once left-turning cars tuck into dedicated bays, the left through lane avoids curb-driveway slowdowns on the right.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.question_text: What traffic relationship do white pavement lines indicate?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.teaching_text: Seeing white dashes beside you confirms adjacent lanes move with you rather than head-on toward you.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.question_text: What traffic relationship do yellow pavement lines indicate?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.teaching_text: Yellow paint on your left warns instantly that crossing that stripe puts you into oncoming traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.question_text: What maneuver does a broken pavement line permit, and under what condition?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.teaching_text: Dashed stripes mark zones with adequate sight distance, though you must still verify clear traffic before crossing.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.question_text: What does a solid white lane line warn drivers about passing or changing lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.teaching_text: Solid white stripes guard intersection approaches and merge zones where last-second lane hops cause sideswipes.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.question_text: What does a solid yellow line prohibit, and what single turning exception is allowed?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.teaching_text: Solid yellow bans overtaking and lane shifts while still letting drivers turn left into or out of driveways, alleys, or private roads.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.question_text: When a center stripe pairs a solid yellow line with a broken line, when are you prohibited from passing?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.teaching_text: A solid yellow stripe next to your lane means sight distance ahead in your direction is too short to overtake.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.question_text: Even when the solid yellow line sits on the opposing side and broken yellow is on yours, what is still required to pass?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.teaching_text: Permissive paint only confirms road geometry allows passing, never that oncoming traffic is absent right now.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.question_text: What passing rule applies where double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.teaching_text: Two solid yellow stripes forbid overtaking from both directions because neither traffic stream has safe passing sightlines.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.question_text: What three actions should you take upon seeing an advance railroad crossing warning sign?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.teaching_text: Round advance warnings appear well ahead of the rails so you can shed speed smoothly before tracks come into view.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.question_text: What letters and line are painted on the pavement approaching a railroad crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.teaching_text: Large white R-X-R letters warn your eyes on the asphalt before a thick stop bar marks the safe clearance boundary.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.question_text: Where must you hold your vehicle while waiting for a train to pass?
sec10-card-sec10-R21.teaching_text: Freight cars overhang wider than the steel rails, so creeping past the stop bar puts your hood inside the strike zone.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.question_text: Which standard traffic sign does a white X-shaped railroad crossbuck act like?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.teaching_text: Trains cannot swerve or stop quickly, so every crossbuck legally obligates road traffic to yield right-of-way.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.question_text: What actions must you take when approaching a crossing marked by a railroad crossbuck?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.teaching_text: Passive rural crossings lack gates or bells, making your own eyes, ears, and reduced speed the only train defense.

sec10-card-sec10-R24.question_text: What does a small number plaque mounted directly below a railroad crossbuck tell you?
sec10-card-sec10-R24.teaching_text: Knowing more than one set of rails crosses the road warns you that a passing train can hide a second train.

sec10-card-sec10-R25.question_text: What must you do when red lights are flashing at a railroad crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-R25.teaching_text: Trying to beat active red crossing signals misjudges deceptive locomotive closing speed with fatal results.

sec10-card-sec10-R26.question_text: Before driving across a multi-track railroad crossing, what must you confirm?
sec10-card-sec10-R26.teaching_text: Pulling forward the instant one caboose clears often puts cars straight into a fast train on the adjacent track.

sec10-card-sec10-R27.question_text: Where must you stop as soon as railroad crossing lights begin to flash at a gated crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-R27.teaching_text: Stopping well short of the gate path prevents getting pinned on the tracks beneath the descending arm.

sec10-card-sec10-R28.question_text: At a gated crossing, what three conditions must all be met before you start across the tracks?
sec10-card-sec10-R28.teaching_text: Crossing while bells or lights stay active after gates budge risks meeting a second train re-triggering the circuit.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Where must you stop after a crash involving you, and how long must you stay?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Leaving before officers arrive and finish questioning everyone involved turns an accident into a serious hit-and-run offense.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: What two immediate steps must you take if anyone is hurt in a crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Prompt basic aid and immediate EMS dispatch save lives during the critical minutes right after impact.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: When is the only situation you should move an injured crash victim?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Lifting someone with hidden neck or spinal trauma can cause permanent paralysis unless a secondary crash threatens their life.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: Why must you alert oncoming and approaching vehicles right after a collision?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Unwarned drivers rounding curves or hills at highway speed can slam into disabled cars and responders.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: Whose names and addresses should you gather at a crash scene?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Independent witnesses leave scenes quickly, yet their statements often settle disputed fault claims later.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: Which three personal and credential details must you record from the other driver?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Verifying the driver's exact license number alongside their name and address prevents fake contact info at the roadside.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: Which five details about the other vehicle should you write down after a crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Recording exact vehicle descriptors, visible impact damage, and plate characters keeps claims accurate and prevents padded repair bills.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: What financial-responsibility detail must you record from the other driver at a crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Knowing the other motorist's insurance carrier right away lets claims adjusters verify liability coverage without delay.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: Which three crash outcomes require you to contact law enforcement in Wyoming?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Modern bumper sensors and paint easily exceed one thousand dollars, making police notification mandatory in most real-world crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: When must you give your crash details to investigating police officers?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Sharing accurate facts right at the scene lets officers document fresh evidence before vehicles move or memories fade.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: Who completes the official crash report and which WYDOT office receives it?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Investigating officers compile the formal state crash record and transmit it directly to WYDOT's Accident Records Section.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: What must you do first if you strike unattended property and cannot locate the owner?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Placing a secure, easy-to-spot written notice fulfills your initial duty when nobody is around to exchange details.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: Which five contact and credential items must appear on a note left on damaged unattended property?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Leaving full contact numbers plus both your driver-license and license-plate numbers proves good-faith accountability.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: Besides your identity details, what three crash facts must an unattended-property note state?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Documenting exact date, time, and observed damage protects both you and the owner if someone else hits the car later.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: After leaving a complete note on damaged unattended property, whom else must you notify?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Wind or rain can ruin a windshield note, so reporting to the nearest police agency locks in proof you complied.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: What three actions may a police officer take if your vehicle appears to have unsafe equipment?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Officers have legal authority to pull over defective cars, demand immediate fixes, and cite operators driving unsafe equipment.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: Which five vehicle lighting systems must stay in proper working order?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Burned-out exterior bulbs hide your car in darkness or leave following traffic guessing when you slow or turn.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: Which two braking systems on your vehicle must be kept in good operating condition?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Healthy service brakes stop you in traffic while a working parking brake holds on grades and backs up hydraulic failure.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: Which three visibility, warning, and restraint items must function properly on your vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Clear mirrors spot hazards, a crisp horn warns others, and intact seat belts keep occupants inside during crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: Which five glass, traction, and underbody components must remain in good condition?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Cracked glass, streaking blades, bald tires, or leaking exhaust pipes create blind driving, skids, or deadly cabin fumes.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: Where do you look to find the correct inflation pressure recommended for your vehicle's tires?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Tire sidewalls print maximum cold burst pressure rather than the vehicle maker's balanced grip-and-ride target.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: What tool should you use to check your tire inflation accurately?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Radial tires can lose half their pressure while still looking round to the naked eye.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: What should you do if your gauge reads higher than the door-jamb tire pressure recommendation?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Overinflated tires crown in the center, shrinking the rubber contact patch and accelerating center-tread wear.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: What should you do when measured tire pressure sits below your vehicle's recommended number?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Running low pressure flexes sidewalls excessively, building blowout heat and sluggish emergency steering.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: How often should you inspect your tires for tread wear and sidewall damage?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Catching bulges, nails, or uneven wear before sustained highway heat prevents high-speed tread separation.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: How do you hold and place a penny to check your tire tread depth?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: Testing the shallowest groove ensures worn alignment edges cannot hide behind deeper ribs elsewhere on the tire.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: What visual result in the handbook's penny test means your tire tread passes?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: Seeing all of Lincoln's head exposed means grooves are too shallow to channel water away at road speed.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: How does driving on tread shallower than the penny-test threshold affect your car?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: Worn grooves cannot evacuate rain or slush, triggering early hydroplaning and long winter skids.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: How do a motorcyclist's legal rights and duties compare with those of car and truck drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Treating motorcycles as full legal vehicles prevents right-of-way cutoffs at intersections and merges.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: What two visual challenges make motorcycles tricky for other drivers to read in traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: A narrow single-headlight silhouette tricks the human eye into thinking a bike is farther away and slower than reality.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: What must you do before turning left in front of an oncoming motorcycle?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: Left turns across oncoming motorcycles cause a huge share of fatal bike crashes when drivers misread closing speed.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: Why must you wait before pulling out ahead of a motorcycle displaying a turn signal?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Pulling out on a blinking lamp alone is deadly if the rider forgot to cancel a signal from an earlier corner.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: Why might a motorcycle's turn signal keep flashing long after a lane change or turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: Unlike passenger cars with steering-column return cams, many motorcycles keep blinking until the rider presses the switch.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: May you drive alongside a motorcycle inside the same lane if the lane is wide or the rider hugs one edge?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: Riders need the entire lane width to lean through curves and swerve around potholes or wind gusts.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.question_text: For what three reasons do motorcyclists intentionally shift left or right inside their lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.teaching_text: Smart riders constantly adjust lane position to escape blind spots, spot traffic ahead, and miss oil or debris.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.question_text: Which six weather or roadway conditions can force a motorcyclist to adjust speed or direction suddenly?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.teaching_text: Two narrow tires react violently to slick spots, gusts, tracks, steel bridge decks, and pavement grooves that cars barely feel.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.question_text: Must you yield to pedestrians in an intersection crosswalk area when no white lines are painted?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.teaching_text: Every street corner forms a legal crosswalk extension whether or not city paint crews striped the asphalt.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.question_text: What two adjustments should you make near schools when pedestrians are around?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.teaching_text: Slower speed plus wider spacing gives you crucial stopping room around distracted student groups.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.question_text: What unpredictable behavior must you anticipate from children near neighborhoods or schools?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.teaching_text: Young children chase balls or friends without judging closing vehicle speed or checking traffic first.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.question_text: Which side of the road should you walk on if a breakdown forces you onto a road without sidewalks?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.teaching_text: Walking on the left facing oncoming cars lets you see drifting headlights early and step clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F41.question_text: What clothing choice helps drivers spot you if you must walk along a road after dark?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.teaching_text: Dark jackets blend into unlit rural asphalt until low-beam headlights are already dangerously close.

sec11-card-sec11-F42.question_text: What rights and duties apply to bicyclists, and where on the pavement must they normally ride?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.teaching_text: Cyclists follow vehicle traffic laws while riding as close to the right edge as safety and road debris allow.

sec11-card-sec11-F43.question_text: Even though a car may legally fit beside a bicycle in one lane, what does the handbook advise?
sec11-card-sec11-F43.teaching_text: Just because bumper and handlebars technically fit inside twelve feet does not leave survival margin if either wobbles.

sec11-card-sec11-F44.question_text: Which three roadside hazards might force a bicyclist to swerve suddenly into your path?
sec11-card-sec11-F44.teaching_text: Drain grates, rocks, and swinging parked-car doors can flip a narrow bike tire unless the rider dodges left.

sec11-card-sec11-F45.question_text: What lighting equipment must a bicycle carry after dark, and what caution remains for drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-F45.teaching_text: Small battery lamps and passive reflectors are far dimmer than car taillights, so bikes stay hard to spot.
sec11-card-sec11-F45.must_match_memory_hook: Front light, rear reflectors, still dim

visual_sync.text_span: Front light, rear reflectors, still dim

sec11-card-sec11-F46.question_text: Where should you actively direct your eyes at night to avoid hitting poorly lit cyclists?
sec11-card-sec11-F46.teaching_text: Scanning along the right pavement edge catches pedaling silhouettes before tiny reflectors finally glint.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: What maximum speed does a slow-moving-vehicle emblem tell you the vehicle ahead can travel?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Closing on a twenty-five-mile-per-hour tractor from highway speed eats up gap distance in mere seconds.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Do slow-moving farm or maintenance vehicles have a legal right to use public roadways?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Impatient tailgating or blind passing around legal ranch and farm machinery causes preventable rural head-on crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: In which five driving maneuvers do tractor-trailers handle very differently from passenger cars?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Eighty-thousand-pound combinations accelerate slowly, climb grades slowly, swing wide on turns, and need long braking room.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Which active-light vehicles, speeds, and roadside positions trigger Wyoming's fuller Move Over rule?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Wyoming protects not just patrol cars, but municipal, utility, construction, and maintenance crews stopped or creeping near lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: How soon must you carry out your Move Over lane change or slowdown once you spot a covered vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Waiting until the last hundred feet traps you in adjacent traffic and leaves roadside workers exposed to mirror wash.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: What happens if a police officer's hand or flare directions conflict with standard Move Over lane separation?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Officers managing a live crash scene know which lanes hold debris or victims and direct traffic accordingly.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: On a highway with two or more same-direction lanes, where must you position your car under Move Over?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Putting at least one empty travel lane between your car and flashing roadside rigs shields crews from sideswipes.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: On a two-lane road posted at 45 mph or higher, how much must you slow down for a Move Over vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: When you cannot give an empty lane on a high-speed two-lane highway, dropping twenty below cuts crash energy dramatically.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: Who can be injured or killed in a wildlife collision on rural Wyoming highways?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Striking deer, elk, or moose at highway speed can crush windshields and roofs, injuring or killing occupants inside.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: Although animal strikes occur all year, during which two seasons do they peak?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Seasonal herd migrations in spring and autumn send thousands of deer, pronghorn, and elk across Wyoming highways.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: How should you respond whenever you pass a yellow deer-crossing warning sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: Highway biologists place crossing signs at proven herd corridors where animals step onto pavement repeatedly.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.question_text: Where should your eyes search when watching for wildlife along rural roads?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.teaching_text: Spotting grazing animals in right-of-way ditches gives you braking seconds before they bolt onto the asphalt.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.question_text: How should you use your headlights at night to spot roadside animals earlier?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.teaching_text: High beams throw light far farther down dark shoulders and ditches whenever no oncoming or leading cars are near.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.question_text: Which two natural landscape features call for extra wildlife alertness?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.teaching_text: Timber cover and creek bottoms attract deer, elk, and moose right up to highway shoulders for shelter and drinking.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.question_text: Which two times of day combine animal feeding movement with poor driver visibility?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.teaching_text: Low sun angles and twilight shadows hide brown coats right when herds move most actively to feed.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.question_text: What subtle visual glint ahead at night often reveals an animal before its body appears?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.teaching_text: Animal retinas bounce headlight beams back like tiny twin reflectors long before dark fur stands out.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.question_text: What three actions should you take when you spot an animal standing on or beside the road?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.teaching_text: Shedding speed, flashing brake lights to warn cars behind, and honking urges the animal off the road without a rear-ender.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.question_text: When can you brake much harder for an animal in the road?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.teaching_text: Knowing your rearview mirror is empty lets you use full safe braking power without getting slammed from behind.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.question_text: Why shouldn't you flash your headlights at an animal standing in the roadway?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.teaching_text: Strobe-like high-beam flashes dazzle nocturnal eyes and lock deer motionless right in your lane.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.question_text: What must you do, and avoid doing, if hitting an animal in your lane becomes unavoidable?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.teaching_text: Violent swerves launch vehicles into oncoming trucks, trees, or rollovers far deadlier than a straight, braked impact.

sec11-card-sec11-R21.question_text: Whom should you notify after hitting an animal, and when is reporting especially urgent?
sec11-card-sec11-R21.teaching_text: A dark carcass left lying in a highway lane can launch the next approaching car or motorcycle into a fatal rollover.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: How does defensive driving define a critical object?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Spotting people, vehicles, animals, or obstacles early gives your brain time to plan smooth adjustments instead of panic swerves.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: How do you carry out the Identify step of defensive driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Active visual searching catches developing conflicts down the block before brake lights flash directly in front of you.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Once you identify a critical object, what mental forecast should you make?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Assuming another road user will make the riskiest believable mistake ensures you are never caught off guard.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: If you spot someone climbing into a parked car ten to fifteen seconds ahead, what should you prepare for?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Drivers eager to leave curb spots frequently pull straight into traffic without checking mirrors or blind zones.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: What priority should guide every defensive-driving decision?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Insisting on legal right-of-way against a distracted driver still lands both vehicles in a wreck.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: What three qualities define a proper Execute maneuver in IPDE?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Jerky, last-second braking or steering upsets tire traction and startles drivers behind you into secondary hits.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: Where must you scan during IPDE driving, and what else must you do with surrounding motorists?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Combining forward and cross-street vision with clear signals keeps hazards visible in both directions.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: Besides scanning and signaling, how does defensive driving manage space and competing hazards?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Maintaining buffer room lets you tackle hazards one by one or favor the deadlier danger when pinched.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: How many seconds ahead of your vehicle does the handbook say you should scan?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Looking a quarter-mile ahead on highways or a full city block in town reveals trouble while gentle slowing still works.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: How do you check in real time how many seconds ahead your eyes are scanning?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Counting thousand-one, thousand-two toward a sign or pole replaces guesswork with an exact time horizon.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: What count confirms you are looking far enough ahead during the forward-scan check?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Reaching your chosen landmark before ten seconds means your eyes are staring too close to your front hood.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: What environmental conditions, controls, and road users should your scan take in?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Tunnel vision on the bumper ahead misses slick patches, warning signs, lane arrows, and curb pedestrians.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: What bad habit usually explains why a driver keeps getting startled by sudden traffic events?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Staring right over the hood turns predictable red lights and merges into sudden last-second emergencies.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: When should you classify people, vehicles, or animals off to the side of the road as critical objects?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Anything along the shoulder capable of stepping, rolling, or bolting toward your lane demands immediate speed or lane prep.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: What specific search should a school warning sign trigger immediately?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Spotting a school pentagon tells you to sweep sidewalks and parked cars for children about to dart across.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: Why is timing so critical when communicating your plans to other drivers?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Flicking a blinker mid-swerve gives surrounding drivers zero seconds to ease off the gas or clear space.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: How can making eye contact help when right-of-way feels unclear?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Locking eyes with a waiting pedestrian or cross-street driver confirms they actually see your car before anyone moves.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: What message can clear hand motions send to another driver or pedestrian?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: A calm wave removes hesitation at low-speed corners when you choose to yield right-of-way.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: What can your vehicle's placement inside a lane communicate to traffic around you?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: Moving cleanly toward the turn edge of your lane reinforces your blinker and signals your upcoming turn.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: How many seconds before a turn does the defensive-communication section say to signal?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Four to five seconds of flashing amber or hand signal lets trailing drivers adjust following distance smoothly.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: What two things does touching the brake pedal lightly well ahead of a planned stop accomplish?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Illuminating red brake lamps early wakes up following drivers while gently shedding momentum before hard braking.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: How does getting into the proper turn lane well ahead of an intersection help other motorists?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Lining up early prevents last-second cross-lane dives that catch neighboring drivers completely off guard.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: How should you use the horn to let an unaware driver, cyclist, or walker know you are there?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: A quick tap gets attention politely whereas a long angry blast startles people into unpredictable panic moves.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: Where should you position your car relative to other vehicles so your presence is unmistakable?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Cruising where drivers can see your headlights in their mirrors keeps them from drifting across your hood.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: Why do defensive drivers keep a four-sided space cushion around the entire car?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Open space around all four bumpers gives you a ready braking or steering escape route when somebody blunders.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: Why does the handbook measure following distance in seconds instead of car lengths?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Estimating ten car lengths at highway speed is error-prone, while time-in-seconds scales distance automatically as speed climbs.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: How do you start the fixed-point count to measure your following time behind a vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Using a shadow, sign, or crack passed by the lead car's rear bumper anchors an exact timing start.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: What does it mean if your front bumper reaches the reference mark before you finish counting two seconds?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Arriving before two seconds elapse proves you lack minimum reaction distance if the lead driver slams the brakes.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: How much following time does Wyoming's length formula require per twenty feet of vehicle length?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Longer rigs and towed loads take deeper space to stop, adding two seconds for every twenty-foot increment.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: What is the minimum baseline following interval for a standard passenger car in ideal conditions?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: A standard sedan sits under twenty feet long, setting two seconds as your bare-minimum dry-day buffer.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: Why must you add extra following time whenever towing a boat or utility trailer?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Extra tongue weight and overall rig length stretch braking distances well beyond solo passenger-car stops.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: Which three driving conditions require doubling a car's following interval to four seconds?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Wet asphalt lowers tire grip, heavy cargo stretches braking, and darkness shortens headlight sight distance.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: How many seconds of following time should a passenger car keep on snow- and slush-covered roads?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Packed snow and slush slash braking traction so severely that a normal two-second gap guarantees a slide-in crash.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: How much following time should you maintain when ice covers the roadway?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Glare ice offers almost zero friction, requiring four times normal dry-road spacing to coast down safely.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: How does a tailgater behind your bumper limit your own emergency options ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Slamming your brakes for a hazard ahead guarantees the close follower behind will ram your trunk.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: Which three early cues should you use to warn a tailgater before slowing or turning?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Giving a tailgater extra visual notice prevents abrupt speed drops that trigger rear-end impacts.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: How should you adjust your front following distance when another driver is tailgating you?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Opening extra room ahead lets you brake gradually for both your car and the impatient driver behind.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: What simple lane move clears a tailgater off your bumper on a multilane highway?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Shifting smoothly into the right lane puts impatient speeders ahead of you instead of glued to your bumper.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: How can easing your speed help deal with a tailgater?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.teaching_text: Slowing gently in a safe passing zone makes overtaking shorter and easier so the tailgater moves on.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.question_text: How do vehicles or barriers on both sides limit your emergency choices?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.teaching_text: With both flanks blocked, you lose lateral swerve room and can only brake or accelerate straight ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.question_text: What positioning mistake next to a bicyclist must you avoid?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.teaching_text: Staying parallel with a cyclist eliminates side cushion for both of you if road debris appears.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.question_text: Why should you avoid cruising right next to cars in adjacent lanes on multilane streets?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.teaching_text: Dropping back or pulling ahead into staggered pockets keeps an open swerve lane beside you at all times.

sec12-card-sec12-R15.question_text: How much lateral separation should you maintain from oncoming vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.teaching_text: Combined closing speed doubles head-on impact violence, making every extra foot from the centerline priceless.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.question_text: Which two blind-spot situations must you actively avoid in traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.teaching_text: Adjusting pace slightly keeps you out of neighboring blind zones while clearing cars lingering unseen beside your own quarter panels.

sec12-card-sec12-R17.question_text: How should you position your car when driving alongside a row of parked vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-R17.teaching_text: A door-width cushion prevents clipping swinging car doors or pedestrians stepping from between bumpers.

sec12-card-sec12-R18.question_text: How do defensive drivers handle two or more road hazards whenever possible?
sec12-card-sec12-R18.teaching_text: Adjusting speed so you never meet two threats at the exact same spot cuts crash complexity in half.

sec12-card-sec12-R19.question_text: In the handbook's oncoming-truck and roadside-jogger scenario, how do you avoid meeting both at once?
sec12-card-sec12-R19.teaching_text: Easing off or adjusting pace lets the oncoming truck clear before you reach the jogger so you have plenty of lane room.

sec12-card-sec12-R20.question_text: What kind of escape space does separating hazards open up for your vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-R20.teaching_text: Clearing one flank before reaching the remaining hazard preserves lateral swerve room if something goes wrong.

sec12-card-sec12-R21.question_text: When two hazards cannot be separated in time, how do you allocate your space?
sec12-card-sec12-R21.teaching_text: Compromising favors the more unpredictable or severe threat with the larger lateral cushion.

sec12-card-sec12-R22.question_text: Between oncoming cars on your left and a child bicyclist on your right, which is the greater danger and why?
sec12-card-sec12-R22.teaching_text: Experienced oncoming drivers track straight in their lane, whereas a young rider can wobble or swerve without warning.

sec12-card-sec12-R23.question_text: Where in your lane should you position your car when trapped between oncoming traffic and a child cyclist?
sec12-card-sec12-R23.teaching_text: Shifting closer to the center stripe trades a predictable left gap for crucial extra feet beside the child.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: Which four nighttime challenges combine after dark to demand sharper driver alertness?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Open Wyoming highways stack oncoming headlight glare and sudden deer crossings right when darkness narrows your sightlines.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: Between what exact evening and morning times does Wyoming law require headlights?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Twilight flattens contrast long before pitch dark, making that thirty-minute buffer after sunset and before sunrise a favorite test item.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: At what forward sight distance do dim light or bad weather legally trigger headlight use?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Blowing snow, rain, or dust can erase gray vehicles inside a thousand feet even at midday.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: Why should you switch on low-beam headlights early as evening light begins to fade?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: At dusk your eyes may still read the road fine while oncoming drivers struggle to spot an unlit hood.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: Can you legally drive with only your parking lights switched on when headlights are required?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Test questions bait drivers who click one notch to amber marker lamps during dusk or storms instead of full low beams.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: How should you adjust your following gap whenever darkness or weather cuts visibility?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Spotting brake lights late steals reaction margin, so stretching your forward cushion prevents chain-reaction rear-end hits.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: Above what speed in the handbook's night illustration does stopping distance outrun headlight reach?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Outrunning your beam means a dark calf or stalled trailer appears inside your lights too late to halt safely.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: Where do high beams belong at night, and which three situations call for low beams?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: High beams light open rural stretches far ahead, whereas town streetlights or nearby windshields turn bright beams into blinding glare.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: How many feet and roughly how many seconds before meeting an oncoming vehicle must you dim high beams?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Dropping to low beams four to five seconds early keeps oncoming drivers from being blinded right before passing your fender.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: Within what distance behind a vehicle ahead must you switch headlights to their lowest beam?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Blasting high beams into a lead car's rearview and side mirrors dazzles that driver from behind.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: How must your low-beam headlights be aimed whenever you drive?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Heavy trunk cargo or misaligned mounts tilt low beams skyward until they blind oncoming traffic like brights.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: How should you clean your windshield to cut nighttime glare from approaching headlights?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Interior cabin film scatters oncoming beams into a milky halo even when exterior washer spray clears bugs.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: Why does wiping road grime off your headlight lenses matter before night travel?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Winter slush and highway road salt coat plastic lenses fast, cutting down the usable light reaching dark pavement.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: What happens if you lock your gaze onto your own bright headlight patch instead of moving your eyes?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Fixing your eyes on one bright patch triggers highway hypnosis, tired eyes, and missed hazards along dark shoulders.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: What roadside hazards and cross-street clues should you actively scan for after dark?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Sweeping side approaches catches glowing animal eyes on shoulders and headlight wash from side-road cars before they enter.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: What two clues can you read by watching the lights of vehicles traveling ahead of you at night?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Shifting or brightening taillights reveal hills, curves, braking, or lane drifts well before your own headlights reach that spot.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: Which headlight setting belongs in fog, and what auxiliary front lamps can help?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: High beams bounce straight off suspended water droplets into a blinding white wall right in front of your hood.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: When is it appropriate to switch on bright red rear fog lights?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Intense red rear fog lamps pierce thick mist to prevent rear-end hits, whereas running them on clear nights dazzles followers.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: What must you do with rear fog lights as soon as visibility clears up?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Leaving bright rear fog bulbs glowing in clear air masks your brake lights and glares at trailing drivers.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: What must you monitor around you while trimming your normal speed in fog?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Dropping speed sensibly while tracking faster or slower vehicles nearby helps avoid sudden closing-speed surprises in thick mist.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.question_text: A speed gap above how many miles per hour from surrounding traffic creates high crash danger in fog?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.teaching_text: Closing at more than fifteen miles per hour faster or slower gives drivers emerging from fog almost no braking margin.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.question_text: What should you do if dense fog threatens to create a wide speed mismatch with surrounding traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.teaching_text: Parking clear of travel lanes at a rest area or exit beats creeping along highway lanes where fast trucks loom.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.question_text: When fog cuts forward sight below how many seconds ahead should you consider pulling off to stop?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.teaching_text: Seeing fewer than ten seconds ahead leaves too little preview window to spot stalled rigs before committing to brake.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.question_text: What targets should you scan for in poor visibility while maximizing your space cushion?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.teaching_text: Dim taillights, roadside walkers, and creeping cars blend into gray mist unless you stretch following space and scan constantly.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: Why must you lower your speed as soon as pavement turns slick?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: Reduced tire friction means even alert braking needs far more pavement to shed momentum before an obstacle.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.question_text: How many seconds of following distance should a passenger car keep in rain?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.teaching_text: Wet asphalt and wiper spray slow down both perception and tire grip, turning a dry two-second gap into four.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.question_text: Which headlight beam should you run whenever driving through rain?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.teaching_text: Low beams cut through rain spray without reflecting glare back off falling drops while lighting your taillights too.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.question_text: What visual sign on your glass tells you it is time for new wiper blades?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.teaching_text: Hardened rubber edges smear oily road spray across your sightline right when oncoming headlights hit wet glass.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.question_text: Why is the first thirty minutes of a rainstorm especially slick on paved roads?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.teaching_text: Light early showers mix with weeks of dripped grease and dust into a slick film before heavy rain washes it away.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.question_text: What physically happens beneath your tires when a car begins hydroplaning?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.teaching_text: Once water wedges tires completely off the asphalt, steering and braking drop near zero like gliding on ice.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.question_text: What straightforward driver adjustment helps keep tires from hydroplaning in rain?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.teaching_text: Slower rotation gives tire tread grooves enough time to channel standing water aside and bite solid pavement.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.question_text: What traction equipment does the handbook recommend for snow and ice to cut skids and braking distance?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.teaching_text: Cold-weather rubber compounds and tire chains bite packed Wyoming snow where summer treads harden and slide.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.question_text: What kinds of throttle, brake, or wheel inputs must you avoid on snow or ice?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.teaching_text: Abrupt gas, hard braking, or sharp wheel tugs instantly break fragile winter tire traction and start a spin.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.question_text: Which two roadway spots freeze earliest and hold black ice longest?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.teaching_text: Cold air chills bridge decks from above and below while tree or canyon shadows block warming sun on dry-looking stretches.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.question_text: To how many seconds does the handbook triple a passenger car's forward cushion on snow?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.teaching_text: Exam items pair four seconds for rain, six for snow, and eight for ice as escalating winter cushions.

sec13-card-sec13-F36.question_text: To how many seconds does the handbook quadruple a passenger car's forward cushion on ice?
sec13-card-sec13-F36.teaching_text: Glazed ice offers minimal braking grip, requiring four times normal dry spacing so you can coast down gently.

sec13-card-sec13-F37.question_text: Why must you scrape and defog all vehicle windows rather than peeking through a tiny porthole?
sec13-card-sec13-F37.teaching_text: Snow-covered side and rear glass hides blind-spot traffic and blocks eye contact with walkers and merging drivers.

sec13-card-sec13-F38.question_text: How should you shed speed before reaching a stop or turn on snow or ice?
sec13-card-sec13-F38.teaching_text: Finishing gentle straight-line deceleration early leaves all available tire grip dedicated to turning your front wheels.

sec13-card-sec13-F39.question_text: Why must you keep your wheels from locking up during winter braking?
sec13-card-sec13-F39.teaching_text: Sliding tires plow straight ahead along momentum regardless of how far you turn the steering wheel.

sec13-card-sec13-F40.question_text: What rule applies to using cruise control on snow-packed or icy roads?
sec13-card-sec13-F40.teaching_text: Cruise control keeps feeding power when drive tires hit slick patches, spinning wheels faster right when you need lift-off.

sec13-card-sec13-F41.question_text: Which vehicles face the greatest danger in strong Wyoming winds, and what is the primary defense?
sec13-card-sec13-F41.teaching_text: Broad side panels on campers, trucks, and towed trailers catch crosswind gusts like sails unless speed drops.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: What steering surprise should you brace for when emerging from a canyon, cut, or overpass into open plain?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Sudden crosswinds slam the side of your car the moment rock cuts or trees stop blocking gusts.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: How can passing or meeting a large semi-truck or bus affect your steering in windy conditions?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: A semi pushes a bow wave of air and blocks crosswinds briefly, tugging your car sideways at both ends.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: When do crosswind gusts pose an extra-high threat to lane control?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: A side gust that barely nudges tires on dry asphalt can push a car sideways across wet or icy lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: What two steps does the handbook advise whenever a Wyoming blizzard threatens?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Ground blizzards drop visibility to zero and close interstates fast, so checking severe-weather alerts before leaving saves lives.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: Why must you stay with your car rather than walking away if stranded or ditched in a blizzard?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Blowing whiteouts erase footprints and landmarks in yards, whereas highway crews easily spot a full-sized vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: How should you set a window if trapped inside a vehicle during a blizzard?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Cracking a downwind window slightly vents stale cabin air and guards against invisible exhaust buildup.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: How should you run the engine for warmth while stranded in snow, and what outside check is critical?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Drifting snow packed around an exhaust pipe forces lethal carbon monoxide straight up into an idling cabin.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: What physical habit inside a stranded winter vehicle helps keep your body warm?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: Gentle limb movement keeps warm blood circulating to fingers and toes without stepping outside into freezing wind.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: Which two vehicle lights help plows and rescuers spot a stranded car, including after dark?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: A tiny interior dome bulb draws very little battery power at night while making a snow-covered cabin glow.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.question_text: If multiple occupants are stranded together in a blizzard, how should they handle sleep?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.teaching_text: Keeping one person awake spots passing snowplows, monitors cabin air, and checks everyone for hypothermia signs.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.question_text: What two physical dangers must stranded drivers avoid during a winter storm?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.teaching_text: Heavy snow shoveling drenches clothing in sweat that chills rapidly and strains the heart in subzero wind.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.question_text: With conventional non-anti-lock brakes, how should you work the pedal when an emergency crash looms?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.teaching_text: Releasing and reapplying pedal pulses lets front tires keep rolling just enough to steer around the obstacle.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.question_text: What happens if you stomp and hold unchanging hard pressure on conventional non-anti-lock brakes?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.teaching_text: Clamping non-anti-lock brakes solid freezes wheel rotation and sends the car skidding straight toward the hazard.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.question_text: How should you press an anti-lock brake pedal during an emergency stop, and why?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.teaching_text: Pumping anti-lock brakes defeats the computer valves that pulse wheel grip faster than any human foot.

sec13-card-sec13-R15.question_text: Toward which side should you generally steer if an unavoidable head-on crash threatens?
sec13-card-sec13-R15.teaching_text: Dodging left risks meeting the oncoming driver swerving back into their own lane at combined highway speeds.

sec13-card-sec13-R16.question_text: Why does the evasive turn-away guidance warn against braking while steering hard away?
sec13-card-sec13-R16.teaching_text: Stomping the brakes mid-swerve overloads front tire grip and triggers a loss-of-control skid right when turning matters most.

sec13-card-sec13-R17.question_text: When can accelerating help avoid a side or rear collision, and what comes right after?
sec13-card-sec13-R17.teaching_text: Pulling briskly ahead clears an intersection T-bone or rear-end threat only when open pavement exists in front.

sec13-card-sec13-R18.question_text: If a collision cannot be prevented at all, what impact angle is safer than hitting head-on?
sec13-card-sec13-R18.teaching_text: An angled sideswipe spreads crash forces over longer time and distance instead of stopping both vehicles instantaneously.

sec13-card-sec13-R19.question_text: If you are forced to hit a roadside object to escape a worse crash, what kind should you aim for?
sec13-card-sec13-R19.teaching_text: Brush, snowbanks, or breakaway posts absorb crash energy gradually compared with rigid bridge piers or oncoming trucks.

sec13-card-sec13-R20.question_text: Where must your eyes and primary focus stay if your accelerator pedal sticks down?
sec13-card-sec13-R20.teaching_text: Reaching down to pry at floor mats takes your eyes off highway curves while speed is climbing.

sec13-card-sec13-R21.question_text: If lifting a stuck gas pedal with your toe fails, how do you cut engine power from the wheels?
sec13-card-sec13-R21.teaching_text: Shifting to neutral immediately disconnects the racing engine from your drive wheels while keeping power steering alive.

sec13-card-sec13-R22.question_text: Once neutral frees you from a stuck throttle, when do you switch off the ignition?
sec13-card-sec13-R22.teaching_text: Killing the ignition while still rolling kills power steering and brake assist or locks the column mid-highway.

sec13-card-sec13-R23.question_text: What follow-up step is essential before driving normally again after a throttle sticks?
sec13-card-sec13-R23.teaching_text: A binding cable, iced linkage, or bunched floor mat will jam again at the worst moment until fixed.

sec13-card-sec13-R24.question_text: What immediate mental response is essential the moment your tires start skidding?
sec13-card-sec13-R24.teaching_text: Panic braking or violently whipping the wheel turns a recoverable minor slide into a full spin.

sec13-card-sec13-R26.question_text: Why does the handbook split skid instructions into two separate sections?
sec13-card-sec13-R26.teaching_text: Applying conventional pedal release when you have anti-lock brakes or vice versa wastes precious stopping distance.

sec13-card-sec13-R25.question_text: In a conventional-brake skid caused by hard braking or heavy gas, what pedal move comes first?
sec13-card-sec13-R25.teaching_text: Letting tires roll freely restores lateral cornering grip so your steering inputs actually point the nose.

sec13-card-sec13-R27.question_text: How should you steer while recovering from a skid?
sec13-card-sec13-R27.teaching_text: Pointing smoothly along your intended lane realigns the rear end, whereas cranking too far whips into a counter-skid.

sec13-card-sec13-R28.question_text: What steering adjustment must you prepare for right as a skid straightens out?
sec13-card-sec13-R28.teaching_text: When sliding tires suddenly bite again, lingering steering angle can sling the tail toward the opposite shoulder.

sec13-card-sec13-R29.question_text: Where should you look for specific skid-handling nuances on a front-wheel-drive vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-R29.teaching_text: Front-wheel-drive cars pull and steer with the same axle, so manufacturer guidance explains model-specific traction behavior.

sec13-card-sec13-R30.question_text: What three-part move sums up handling an anti-lock brake emergency?
sec13-card-sec13-R30.teaching_text: Holding firm pedal force lets anti-lock sensors prevent wheel lock while you steer smoothly around the hazard.

sec13-card-sec13-R31.question_text: When should you figure out whether the car you are driving has anti-lock or conventional brakes?
sec13-card-sec13-R31.teaching_text: An emergency leaves zero time to guess whether dashboard warning lamps showed anti-lock brakes at startup.

sec13-card-sec13-R32.question_text: What gearshift and path choices help slow a vehicle if normal foot brakes fail?
sec13-card-sec13-R32.teaching_text: Dropping into lower gears uses engine compression to drag speed down while you aim toward a safe escape area.

sec13-card-sec13-R33.question_text: Why must you keep holding the release lever or button when applying a manual parking brake during brake failure?
sec13-card-sec13-R33.teaching_text: Ratcheting the parking brake locked freezes only the rear wheels, spinning the tail around unless you can ease tension.

sec13-card-sec13-R34.question_text: Once you bring a car with failed brakes to a stop, may you limp it carefully to a repair shop?
sec13-card-sec13-R34.teaching_text: Driving one more block without working service brakes risks rolling helplessly through an intersection or downhill grade.

sec13-card-sec13-R35.question_text: What is your immediate steering priority the instant a tire blows out?
sec13-card-sec13-R35.teaching_text: A shredded tire tugs violently toward the flat side, requiring two firm hands on the wheel to hold lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R36.question_text: How should you handle the gas and brake pedals right after a tire blows out?
sec13-card-sec13-R36.teaching_text: Slamming the brakes during a blowout pitches heavy nose weight onto the damaged wheel and triggers a spin.

sec13-card-sec13-R37.question_text: When is it safe to apply gentle braking and leave the lane after a blowout?
sec13-card-sec13-R37.teaching_text: Waiting until speed drops and steering stabilizes lets you ease safely onto a wide flat shoulder.

sec13-card-sec13-R38.question_text: What reminder applies when jacking up and changing a blown tire beside a road?
sec13-card-sec13-R38.teaching_text: Fast highway traffic passing feet from a jacked car makes firm ground, flashers, and traffic awareness vital.

sec13-card-sec13-R39.question_text: What first warning and speed steps should you take if an oncoming vehicle drifts into your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R39.teaching_text: Shedding speed buys precious extra seconds while flashing headlights can snap a drowsy or distracted driver awake.

sec13-card-sec13-R40.question_text: Where should you position your car if a wrong-way driver keeps closing in your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R40.teaching_text: Hugging the far right edge opens space in the lane without swerving into the oncoming driver's left-hand lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R41.question_text: If an oncoming vehicle still stays in your path and impact threatens, where do you steer?
sec13-card-sec13-R41.teaching_text: Running onto a gravel shoulder or grass ditch is vastly more survivable than a highway head-on collision.

sec13-card-sec13-R42.question_text: Why must you never twist the ignition key to the lock position while your vehicle is rolling?
sec13-card-sec13-R42.teaching_text: Engaging the column pin freezes the steering wheel solid mid-motion so you cannot follow curves or dodge hazards.

sec13-card-sec13-R43.question_text: If your right wheels drop off the paved edge onto a rough shoulder, what immediate posture keeps control?
sec13-card-sec13-R43.teaching_text: Soft gravel and pavement ruts yank at dropped tires, so bracing both hands prevents the wheel wrenching loose.

sec13-card-sec13-R44.question_text: While stabilizing after your wheels leave the pavement, where should you steer and what do you do with the gas?
sec13-card-sec13-R44.teaching_text: Jerking immediately back across a sharp pavement lip at high speed slingshots cars across oncoming traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-R45.question_text: How should you use the brakes while rolling straight along an unpaved shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-R45.teaching_text: Hard braking when left tires sit on asphalt and right tires sit on loose gravel spins the vehicle sideways.

sec13-card-sec13-R46.question_text: Once you have slowed down on the shoulder, what must you check before steering back onto the highway?
sec13-card-sec13-R46.teaching_text: Climbing back onto the travel lane without checking mirrors and oncoming gaps puts you straight into fast traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: Which fleet types count as authorized emergency vehicles under the Wyoming glossary?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: Knowing statutory emergency vehicles extend beyond patrol cars and fire engines ensures you yield promptly whenever sirens approach.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: How does the glossary define a bicycle, and what wheeled devices does it leave out?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Test questions check that scooters and toy push devices fall outside the statutory two-tandem-wheel bicycle definition.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: How does the Wyoming handbook classify bicycles when operating on public roads?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Classifying bicycles as vehicles grants riders lawful road access while holding them to standard traffic duties.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: Are bicycle helmets legally mandatory in Wyoming, and what headgear standard does the handbook recommend?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Even without a statewide helmet mandate, a properly fitted certified helmet dramatically cuts brain-injury risk in crashes.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: Where around your vehicle do glossary blind spots hide from your rearview mirrors?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Assuming flat mirrors reveal everything along both rear quarters causes classic lane-change sideswipes.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.question_text: What physical move must you make to check the blind-spot areas beside your vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.teaching_text: A crisp shoulder glance sweeps the rear-corner pocket that neither inside nor side mirrors can fully capture.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: How does the glossary define a crosswalk?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: Recognizing every legal crossing zone reminds drivers where foot traffic holds statutory right-of-way across lanes.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: Does a legal crosswalk always require painted white stripes on the pavement?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Failing to yield at an unpainted corner crosswalk carries the same legal violation as ignoring bright zebra stripes.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: How do you picture the boundaries of an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: Projecting sidewalk edges straight across the street reveals exactly where your front bumper must stop for walkers.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: What does the glossary mean by a traffic gap?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Waiting for an opening wide enough that approaching drivers need not slam brakes prevents merge and turn crashes.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: In straightforward glossary terms, what is a helmet?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: Protective helmets cushion skull impacts for motorcyclists, moped operators, and cyclists when pavement contact occurs.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.question_text: What is a No-Zone around a large truck or heavy vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.teaching_text: Lingering beside a trailer or tucked tight behind its rear doors hides your car completely from the trucker.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: Who is a self-propelled pedestrian vehicle exclusively built to serve?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: Motorized wheelchairs and disability mobility rigs share pedestrian status rather than ordinary motor-vehicle rules.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: What maximum width in inches does the glossary set for a pedestrian vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.teaching_text: Capping width at forty-eight inches ensures disability mobility devices fit standard sidewalks, curb ramps, and crosswalks.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: What do the letters B A C stand for, and what does the term measure?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: Chemical testing measures bloodstream alcohol concentration objectively regardless of whether a drinker claims to feel fine.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: How does the glossary define vehicle brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: Keeping braking hardware maintained ensures kinetic energy converts reliably into controlled stops whenever hazards appear.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: What makes a person, animal, or vehicle ahead count as a critical object?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Spotting critical objects early lets you adjust throttle, brakes, or lane position smoothly instead of panic-swerving.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: What offense does Wyoming's D W U I abbreviation describe?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: Wyoming uses D W U I to cover impairment by controlled substances right alongside alcohol behind the wheel.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: According to the glossary, what are your tires riding on during hydroplaning?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Standing rain wedges tires off solid pavement so steering and brakes lose road bite until speed drops.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: How does the glossary define an intersection?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Every junction where streets join or cross concentrates turning conflicts, signals, and right-of-way duties.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.question_text: How many lines of vehicles is a single roadway lane built to carry?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.teaching_text: Staying centered inside your single-file strip prevents sideswipes with adjacent traffic or oncoming vehicles.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.question_text: What does a highway median separate, and what materials can form it?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.teaching_text: Physical grass, earth, or concrete dividers buffer opposing highway streams from crossover head-on crashes.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.question_text: May a driver cut across, ride on, or drive over a highway median?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.teaching_text: Cutting across grass or raised medians launches slow dirt-covered vehicles straight into fast left-lane traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.question_text: When does merging traffic happen, and what classic highway spot illustrates it?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.teaching_text: Interstate entrance ramps bring accelerating ramp traffic alongside mainline lanes where smooth speed matching prevents collisions.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.question_text: What power source and transport role define a motor vehicle on public highways?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.teaching_text: Any self-propelled highway machine powered beyond human muscle triggers motor-vehicle traffic and equipment rules.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.question_text: Does the glossary count motorcycles and mopeds as motor vehicles?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.teaching_text: Smaller two-wheeled motorized bikes hold full lane rights and motor-vehicle duties on public streets.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.question_text: What makes an offense count as a moving violation on your driving record?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.teaching_text: Convictions tied to how a rolling vehicle is controlled accumulate toward license suspension thresholds.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.question_text: Which two license-restriction breaches can trigger a moving-violation conviction?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.teaching_text: Driving without prescribed glasses or required outside mirrors counts as an active moving offense rather than paperwork.

sec15-card-sec15-R19.question_text: Which three sequential stages combine to make up total stopping distance?
sec15-card-sec15-R19.teaching_text: Many learners count only tire skids and forget the yards covered while recognizing danger and moving your foot.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: What wheel count, weight range, ID mark, and seat height define a Wyoming multipurpose vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Knowing the three-hundred-pound floor, three-thousand-pound cap, four-wheel minimum, and twenty-four-inch seat height nails tricky glossary items.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: What registration and tag rule applies before operating a multipurpose vehicle on streets or highways?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.teaching_text: Unplated off-road machines stay illegal on public pavement until properly registered and displaying a license plate.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: Which highways ban multipurpose vehicles, and what special rules govern them?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.teaching_text: Light utility rigs lack freeway crash protection and top speed, keeping them off interstates under slow-moving rules.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: Which Wyoming driver-license classes authorize operating a multipurpose vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: Unlike motorcycles that require a dedicated endorsement, any valid Wyoming driver license covers street-legal multipurpose vehicles.

sec15-card-sec15-R14.question_text: Which specific part of a street or highway corridor counts as the roadway?
sec15-card-sec15-R14.teaching_text: Traffic statutes distinguish the traveled driving lanes from adjacent gravel or paved shoulders.

sec15-card-sec15-R15.question_text: Where does a highway shoulder sit, and what two surfaces might it have?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.teaching_text: Expecting either asphalt or loose gravel beside the fog line prepares your steering grip during emergency pull-offs.
