sec15-card-sec15-R16.question_text: Which two practical functions does a highway shoulder serve?
sec15-card-sec15-R16.teaching_text: Shoulders give disabled vehicles refuge outside live lanes while sloping runoff water clear of traveled asphalt.

sec15-card-sec15-R17.question_text: In which directions around your car does a proper space cushion protect you?
sec15-card-sec15-R17.teaching_text: Maintaining clear margin on all four sides preserves braking room ahead and swerve room if someone drifts close.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: At what minimum age and under which three life statuses does a teen qualify as an emancipated minor?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: Exam questions check both the age-seventeen floor and the three qualifying paths of marriage, military service, or court order.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: How does a qualifying teen have emancipated status placed onto a Wyoming license?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: Emancipated status is never automatic until you submit an application and required fee to the licensing agency.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: What payment is mandatory before a suspended or revoked license privilege can be restored?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Even after your suspension calendar expires, driving remains illegal until the reinstatement fee clears and privileges restore.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.question_text: Staying in Wyoming for at least how many days triggers the presence clause of residency?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.teaching_text: Living in Wyoming four months or longer establishes statutory residency requiring state licensing compliance.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.question_text: How does registering to vote in Wyoming affect your driver-licensing resident status?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.teaching_text: Signing onto Wyoming voter rolls immediately counts you as a state resident even before one hundred twenty days pass.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.question_text: How does applying for state public assistance affect whether Wyoming counts you as a resident?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.teaching_text: Seeking resident public benefits claims Wyoming domicile, bringing state driver-license requirements into play.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.question_text: Which outdoor recreation credentials also classify the holder as a Wyoming resident in the handbook?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.teaching_text: Claiming in-state hunting or fishing rates legally declares Wyoming residency for driver-licensing rules too.

sec15-card-sec15-R13.question_text: What does revocation do to your privilege to drive?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.teaching_text: Unlike a temporary pause, revocation cancels your license outright so starting over requires fresh qualification once eligible.

sec15-card-sec15-R18.question_text: How does suspension differ from revocation, and how do privileges come back?
sec15-card-sec15-R18.teaching_text: Suspension holds privileges away temporarily until a set period, required conditions, or both are satisfied.

sec15-card-sec15-R20.question_text: Which Wyoming state agency oversees driver licensing?
sec15-card-sec15-R20.teaching_text: Driver exams, renewals, and records run through state transportation Driver Services offices across Wyoming.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.question_text: Why do standardized sign shapes and background colors matter when snow, glare, or distance blurs text?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.teaching_text: Blowing Wyoming snow or sun glare can hide printed words while an octagon or yellow diamond still reads clearly.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.question_text: What core guidance do painted pavement markings give a driver?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.teaching_text: Center stripes, lane dashes, and edge lines show exactly where your tires belong relative to surrounding traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.question_text: What is the legal force of regulatory traffic signs?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.teaching_text: Speed, turn, and lane regulatory panels state enforceable traffic law rather than optional travel tips.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.question_text: How many sides form an octagon, and which single traffic sign owns it?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.teaching_text: Reserving the eight-sided outline strictly for stop signs lets drivers recognize cross-street priority from any angle.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.question_text: What kind of stop does a red stop sign legally demand?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.teaching_text: Slowing to a rolling creep still counts as running a stop sign and misses cross traffic hidden behind pillars.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.question_text: What action does a downward-pointing triangular sign require toward intersecting or merging vehicles?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.teaching_text: Slowing early at a yield triangle prepares you to halt completely whenever cross or mainline traffic occupies the gap.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.question_text: What is the main job of roadway warning signs?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.teaching_text: Advance warning plates give you early notice to ease off the gas before reaching curves, crossings, or narrow bridges.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.question_text: What geometric outline do most roadway warning signs use?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.teaching_text: Spotting a tilted four-sided diamond down the highway tells you a hazard or change lies ahead.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.question_text: Which kinds of roadway situations can warning signs highlight for extra driver attention?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.teaching_text: Whether flagging sharp curves, active construction, or school zones, warning panels cue immediate speed and eye adjustments.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.question_text: How do ordinary warning-sign colors differ from construction and maintenance warnings?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.teaching_text: Switching from standard yellow to bright orange signals temporary work crews, cones, and altered lanes ahead.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.question_text: Which two core traffic behaviors do rectangular regulatory signs govern?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.teaching_text: Speed-limit plates, one-way arrows, and turn restrictions use crisp rectangles to post binding movement rules.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.question_text: What does a yellow diamond with black symbols or lettering announce?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.teaching_text: High-contrast black icons against yellow reflect headlights sharply at night to warn of curves, merges, or crossings.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.question_text: Which two school-related areas are marked by a five-sided pentagon sign?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.teaching_text: Picture a five-sided schoolhouse silhouette so you immediately drop speed and scan sidewalks for children.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.question_text: What roadway restriction begins right where a pennant-shaped sign stands?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.teaching_text: Mounted on the left shoulder, the sideways pennant warns passing drivers to tuck back right before sightlines vanish.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.question_text: Which specific crossing ahead is announced by a round warning sign?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.teaching_text: Only advance railroad warnings use a full circle, giving you early notice to listen and scan before the tracks.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.question_text: Which painted pavement markings can appear on the lane approaching railroad tracks?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.teaching_text: A thick stop bar shows where to halt clear of gates while the giant X and R R warn early.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.question_text: How can highway engineers combine warnings on the approach to a railroad crossing?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.teaching_text: Pairing upright round signs and crossbucks with asphalt markings ensures drivers catch the warning in fog or traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.question_text: What text and background colors appear on construction signs?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.teaching_text: Sharp black print on fluorescent orange stands out vividly against dirt, concrete, and daytime sky.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.question_text: What kind of conditions do construction and maintenance signs warn drivers to expect?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.teaching_text: Unlike permanent curves, roadwork zones introduce fresh gravel, flaggers, and shifted lanes that change day to day.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.question_text: What is the purpose of the Emergency Notification Sign posted at a railroad crossing?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.teaching_text: Calling the posted railroad dispatch number with the crossing ID lets dispatchers halt oncoming locomotives fast.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.question_text: Which two crossing problems does the handbook give as examples for using the Emergency Notification Sign?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.teaching_text: Reporting a stalled trailer on the rails or malfunctioning signals prevents catastrophic grade-crossing collisions.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.question_text: What three pieces of navigation help do highway guide signs give motorists?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.teaching_text: Clear guide panels let drivers confirm routes early and merge smoothly well ahead of highway splits.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.question_text: While most guide signs use rectangles, which two marker types can wear distinct shapes?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.teaching_text: Distinctive shields and pentagon county markers let travelers tell interstates, national routes, and county roads apart instantly.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.question_text: What determines whether a guide sign uses green, blue, or brown?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.teaching_text: Matching color to message type separates directional route green from blue motorist services and brown recreation sites.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a halt at a steady red traffic light?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.teaching_text: Stopping short of painted lines keeps crosswalks open for walkers and turning clearance open for large trucks.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.question_text: When is turning right on a steady red light lawful in Wyoming?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.teaching_text: Rolling through without halting first or missing a posted no-turn-on-red sign earns a red-light citation.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.question_text: Under what exact street pairing does Wyoming permit a left turn on a red light?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.teaching_text: Turning left on red is legal only from one one-way street onto another one-way street after stopping and yielding.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.question_text: How should you respond when a traffic signal turns steady amber?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.teaching_text: Slamming brakes inside the crosswalk causes rear-end hits, whereas gunning the throttle from far back runs the red.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.question_text: What clearance and yielding rules apply before driving into an intersection on a green light?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.teaching_text: A fresh green never lets you bull forward if blocked lanes would trap you or walkers are still crossing.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.question_text: Which roadside sign shares the exact same legal requirement as a flashing red signal?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.teaching_text: Halt completely before the intersection, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.

sec16-card-sec16-R12.question_text: What does a flashing amber traffic signal require at an intersection or hazard spot?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.teaching_text: Flashing amber marks tricky rural junctions or curves where slowing and scanning prevents cross-traffic surprises.

sec16-card-sec16-R13.question_text: What movement is barred when a traffic signal displays a lighted red arrow?
sec16-card-sec16-R13.teaching_text: Unlike a circular red that may allow turns after stopping, a red arrow flatly forbids turning its way.

sec16-card-sec16-R14.question_text: Which signal often precedes an amber arrow, and what does the amber arrow warn drivers to do?
sec16-card-sec16-R14.teaching_text: Protected turn time is ending, so drivers already turning finish clearing while approaching cars prepare to stop.

sec16-card-sec16-R15.question_text: How may you turn on a green arrow, and who still holds right-of-way inside the intersection?
sec16-card-sec16-R15.teaching_text: Even during a protected arrow phase, late-clearing walkers or vehicles still in the crosswalk keep priority.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: What two dangerous braking behaviors can happen right after your brakes get soaked?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Uneven water film on left versus right rotors yanks steering sideways or slashes stopping power when you need it.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: What quick system check should you run right after driving through deep standing water?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Finding out your pads are waterlogged at the next red light is far too late to pump them dry.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: How do you dry wet brakes safely so normal stopping power returns?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Gentle repeated pedal taps build just enough friction heat to evaporate water off drums and rotors without skidding.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: If mechanical trouble forces you to stop along a road, where must your tires sit?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Leaving two left tires hanging inside a high-speed highway lane invites catastrophic rear-end strikes in low light.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: Which lights should you switch on immediately after pulling onto the shoulder with a breakdown?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Flashing amber lamps warn approaching drivers that your vehicle is stationary rather than moving with highway flow.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: Through which side should occupants step out of a disabled car parked on a shoulder?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Swinging open a traffic-side door steps your body inches from highway mirrors and semi-truck slipstreams.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: Which visual signals on a disabled car tell passing patrols or motorists that you need assistance?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Tying white fabric to a handle or antenna and lifting the hood broadcasts distress without standing near live lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: What does the handbook say about walking down an interstate highway to find help after breaking down?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: High-speed rural Wyoming interstates stretch long miles between exits with fast truck traffic right beside the shoulder.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: Why should you move into a left lane whenever possible while passing a disabled vehicle on the shoulder?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: Startled motorists changing flats or grabbing gear often swing a door wide or step backward toward passing traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: Why is carbon monoxide gas impossible to detect by sight or smell?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Because you cannot see or smell exhaust fumes seeping into a cabin, physical symptoms are often your only clue.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: Which physical warning signs does the handbook link to possible carbon-monoxide poisoning?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Drivers easily mistake early carbon-monoxide drowsiness, nausea, and headaches for ordinary road trip fatigue.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: What two immediate steps must you take if cabin symptoms point to carbon-monoxide exposure?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Stopping exhaust production immediately and flooding the cabin with clean air prevents sudden loss of consciousness behind the wheel.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: What routine maintenance check guards against carbon monoxide entering your car?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Rusted mufflers or cracked underside pipes let lethal fumes seep straight through floorboard seals while driving.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: Why should you avoid sitting parked for long stretches with the motor idling?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Without forward airflow sweeping fumes away, exhaust swirls underneath a parked car and creeps into cabin vents.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: What strict rule applies to starting or warming up a vehicle inside a shut garage?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: An enclosed garage traps concentrated carbon monoxide to lethal concentrations within minutes even before you back out.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: What assumption should you make every single time you approach railroad tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Freight trains run on unscheduled timetables day and night, catching local drivers who assume tracks stay quiet.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: Before rolling onto railroad tracks, what space check on the other side is mandatory?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Following bumper-to-bumper traffic onto rails traps your car across the steel if the line halts ahead.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: When lowered crossing arms close the road, what two things must happen before you drive forward?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: Moving the instant a gate twitches while red lamps still flash risks driving straight into a second train.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: Is driving around a lowered railroad crossing gate ever permitted?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Zigzagging past crossing arms is both illegal and one of the deadliest gambles on the highway.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: At a crossing with more than one set of rails, what check comes before pulling out?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Wyoming freight corridors often run twin mainlines where a passing train hides fast opposing traffic on parallel rails.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: What is your very first priority if your vehicle stalls right on railroad tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Steel cars can be replaced, whereas every heartbeat spent inside a stalled cabin on live rails risks lives.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: Why must you never try restarting or pushing a stalled car off tracks with passengers still seated inside?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: Trains close distance quietly at high speed, leaving trapped riders no time to unbuckle if an impact occurs.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: Which emergency number should you dial immediately once everyone is clear of a car stalled on tracks?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Dispatchers alert rail operators immediately to halt approaching trains before they reach the blocked crossing.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: Which two risky maneuvers are strictly off-limits at a railroad crossing?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Overtaking another car across tracks blocks your view of signals and steals your escape lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: Once a construction flag person halts your lane, when may you start rolling again?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Pulling out early because the lane looks empty risks colliding head-on with hidden dump trucks or opposing traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: How should you adjust speed and visual scanning inside an active construction zone?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: Heavy graders and crew members step near narrow cone lines with noisy machinery masking your approaching car.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: Should you relax your caution in a signed work zone when no crews seem to be working?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: Narrowed shoulders, uneven pavement ledges, and shifted barriers remain hazardous all night and weekend when crews leave.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: Why is sprinting past a semi-truck and darting in ahead of it before a work-zone taper so dangerous?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Loaded tractor-trailers need massive braking distance, so stealing their front buffer right as traffic slows invites disaster.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: Which non-motorized road users count as pedestrians under the handbook definition?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: Remembering skaters and wheelchair users carry full pedestrian protections keeps you yielding properly beyond ordinary walkers.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.question_text: In which five neighborhood or town settings should you expect frequent pedestrian activity?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.teaching_text: Anticipating foot traffic around storefronts, parks, and neighborhoods primes your foot over the brake before someone steps out.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.question_text: How much should you lower speed in areas where pedestrians are likely to appear?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.teaching_text: Parked SUVs and street trees hide stepping walkers until late, so lower pace keeps stopping distance inside sight distance.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.question_text: During which maneuvers and street transitions must you yield right-of-way to pedestrians?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.teaching_text: Drivers pulling across sidewalks into alleys or parking lots often forget walkers on the sidewalk hold priority.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.question_text: Why can swerving violently to miss an animal on the highway be worse than hitting it?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.teaching_text: Whipping the wheel at highway speed rolls SUVs or launches cars head-on into oncoming traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.question_text: If striking a deer or other animal becomes unavoidable, what must stay your top priority throughout?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.teaching_text: Holding the wheel straight and controlled through impact keeps your vehicle upright on the pavement instead of tumbling.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: How must a responsible driver handle personal physical or mental limitations?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Adjusting habits for mild limits or handing over keys when impaired prevents foreseeable crashes.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: How does losing emotional self-control behind the wheel affect your driving safety?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Frustration narrows visual scanning and triggers aggressive tailgating, speed spikes, and missed traffic signals.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: What should you do when intense feelings overwhelm your ability to stay composed?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Cooling down before starting the car beats turning an emotional crisis into a roadway emergency.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: Which two core driving skills suffer when strong grief, rage, or terror takes over?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Intense distress floods working memory, causing drivers to look right at red lights or merging trucks without registering danger.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: Can even everyday mild emotions affect safe driving?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Daydreaming about exciting news or replaying a minor argument pulls mental bandwidth away from traffic scanning.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: How does clear central vision support the safe-driving decision chain?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Identifying a critical object blocks ahead gives your brain calm time to predict its path and respond smoothly.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: What specific danger does healthy side vision help a driver catch?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Peripheral awareness flags cross-street cars, cyclists, and darting kids before your central gaze turns toward them.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: Why does accurate distance judgment matter behind the wheel?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Judging how far away and how fast oncoming cars close determines every safe pass, turn, and lane merge.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: Which two separate nighttime visual abilities does the handbook highlight as part of good vision?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: A driver may see decently under dim streetlights yet stay temporarily blinded after bright oncoming headlights pass.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.question_text: How can drivers compensate when their eyes struggle to focus clearly at distance?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.teaching_text: Properly prescribed corrective lenses restore crisp sign-reading and hazard detection so vision restrictions stay satisfied.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.question_text: How must a driver with reduced side vision compensate, especially before changing lanes?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.teaching_text: Swiveling your neck actively sweeps central vision across side mirrors and blind spots that narrow peripheral sight misses.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.question_text: What does the handbook instruct if a vision limitation cannot be safely overcome?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.teaching_text: Continuing to drive when lenses and habits can no longer reveal hazards endangers everyone sharing the road.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.question_text: What two spacing adjustments help a driver who struggles with distance judgment?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.teaching_text: Building extra cushion behind lead cars and waiting for longer passing gaps offsets misjudged closing speeds.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.question_text: Poor distance judgment makes it harder to predict traffic events how many seconds ahead?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.teaching_text: Struggling to gauge depth clouds your ten-to-fifteen-second visual lead, causing late braking at intersections and merges.

sec14-card-sec14-R15.question_text: While slowing down at night helps weak night vision, driving how much slower than traffic creates its own hazard?
sec14-card-sec14-R15.teaching_text: Crawling ten to fifteen miles per hour under highway speed invites fast-closing drivers to rear-end you in the dark.

sec14-card-sec14-R16.question_text: What two route or schedule choices does the handbook recommend for poor night vision?
sec14-card-sec14-R16.teaching_text: Sticking to bright town streets or daytime errands avoids dark high-speed highways altogether.

sec14-card-sec14-R17.question_text: Where should you aim your gaze when oncoming headlights dazzle eyes with slow glare recovery?
sec14-card-sec14-R17.teaching_text: Tracking the white right fog line keeps your car centered in its lane without staring into blinding beams.

sec14-card-sec14-R18.question_text: What does the handbook name as the single best solution for poor headlight glare recovery?
sec14-card-sec14-R18.teaching_text: Planning errands between sunrise and sunset completely eliminates oncoming headlight dazzle on dark roads.

sec14-card-sec14-R19.question_text: Which roadway sounds can warn you to adjust speed or lane position before your eyes spot trouble?
sec14-card-sec14-R19.teaching_text: Hearing a motorcycle revving in your blind spot or distant train horn stops a disastrous lane change early.

sec14-card-sec14-R20.question_text: Which two equipment aids does the handbook list to help drivers compensate for hearing loss?
sec14-card-sec14-R20.teaching_text: Pairing properly tuned hearing aids with full left-and-right exterior mirrors turns missed sounds into clear visual checks.

sec14-card-sec14-R21.question_text: What scanning habits help drivers with reduced hearing stay safe in traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-R21.teaching_text: Sweeping side mirrors and intersections more often spots flashing emergency strobes before sirens ever register.

sec14-card-sec14-R22.question_text: What two interior factors can cause even a driver with sharp hearing to miss sirens or horns?
sec14-card-sec14-R22.teaching_text: Tight modern door seals combined with blasting speakers drown out emergency sirens until a rig reaches your bumper.

sec14-card-sec14-R23.question_text: How should you set music or podcast volume inside your vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-R23.teaching_text: Moderate cabin volume lets horns, railroad bells, and approaching ambulances cut cleanly through to your ears.

sec14-card-sec14-R24.question_text: How does operating a cell phone behind the wheel affect vehicle control?
sec14-card-sec14-R24.teaching_text: Dividing visual, manual, or mental attention with a phone slows brake reaction and causes lane drift.

sec14-card-sec14-R25.question_text: Does switching a phone call to hands-free eliminate the distraction of talking while driving?
sec14-card-sec14-R25.teaching_text: Exam questions target the myth that keeping both hands on the wheel stops phone conversations from causing mental blindness.

sec14-card-sec14-R26.question_text: What does Wyoming law prohibit regarding electronic text messages while operating a vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-R26.teaching_text: Glancing down to read or type a message at highway pace drives the length of a football field blindfolded.

sec14-card-sec14-R27.question_text: Why must you watch posted city-limit signs regarding cell phone calls across Wyoming?
sec14-card-sec14-R27.teaching_text: Several Wyoming municipalities outlaw handheld phone calls inside city boundaries even where rural state highways allow them.

sec14-card-sec14-R28.question_text: What does the Wyoming Department of Transportation advise doing before making a call or sending a text?
sec14-card-sec14-R28.teaching_text: Stopping safely off the highway lets you handle calls or messages with zero risk of drifting into traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-R29.question_text: How should you handle a phone call that turns long, emotional, or mentally demanding?
sec14-card-sec14-R29.teaching_text: Heated or complex phone talks hijack attention completely, so promise to call back once parked safely.

sec14-card-sec14-R30.question_text: Why should you evaluate your fitness before every drive rather than assuming yesterday's readiness?
sec14-card-sec14-R30.teaching_text: Sleep loss, illness, medication, and stress shift day by day, changing whether you are sharp enough to drive.

sec14-card-sec14-R31.question_text: Who can help you judge whether an illness, medication, or disability compromises safe driving?
sec14-card-sec14-R31.teaching_text: A physician understands how symptoms or prescriptions affect reaction time, vision, and alertness behind the wheel.
